author: filinvadim
body:
## What

Lets links like `warpnet.site/user?id={id}` pop the user's profile in the running desktop app (or prompt the user to install it). Cross-platform: macOS, Windows, Linux. Frontend routing is wired in this PR too.

## How

### Landing snippet — `deep-link-embed.html` (repo root)
A self-contained HTML+CSS+JS embed block, no build tools, no dependencies. Designed for hosts that can't deploy a standalone file or set up rewrites (e.g. Hostinger's "Custom embed code"): paste it into a page published at `/user` and link to it as `warpnet.site/user?id={user_id}`. Parses the id from `?id=` (with `/user/{id}` pathname fallback), fires `warpnet://user/{id}` through a hidden iframe (the only auto-fire technique that doesn't blow up the tab with Chrome's "site can't be reached" interstitial when the scheme is unregistered), and falls back to an Open/Download UI if no app catches it within 1.5s. UA-sniffs the right installer hint. CSS is scoped under `#warpnet-launcher` so the host template's styles are untouched.

### Go — `cmd/node/member/deeplink` (new package)
- `Parse(raw)` → `Link{Kind, ID, Raw}`. Tolerates `warpnet:user/x`, trailing slashes, uppercase scheme, surrounding whitespace. `Link.Raw` keeps the original input so log lines reflect what the OS actually handed us. Rejects unsupported kinds cleanly.
- `FromArgs(os.Args)` finds the first `warpnet://` arg for the cold-start path. Tolerates leading `-`/`--` prefixes (some wrapper scripts produce that form).
- `Register()` claims the scheme per OS:
  - **darwin**: no-op. Declared in `Info.plist` via `wails.json` `info.protocols` (Wails generates `CFBundleURLTypes` from it).
  - **windows**: writes `HKCU\Software\Classes\warpnet\shell\open\command` — no admin needed. Rewritten every launch so a moved .exe stays valid.
  - **linux**: writes `~/.local/share/applications/warpnet.desktop` (with `Exec=%q %u` so paths with spaces survive) + `xdg-mime default` (5s timeout).

### Wiring in `main.go` / `app.go`
- `deeplink.Register()` runs before `wails.Run` (best-effort, warn-only).
- `os.Args` is parsed for a `warpnet://` arg → stashed on `App.deepLink`.
- `Mac.OnUrlOpen` set to do the same — macOS keeps a single process and routes hot clicks through this callback.
- `App.ConsumePendingDeepLink()` is bound for the Vue frontend to pull after login. Both `SetPendingDeepLink` and `ConsumePendingDeepLink` guard against `a.mx == nil` (the cold-start path calls `SetPendingDeepLink` before `startup()` has wired up the mutex).

### Frontend (Vue) — in this PR
- `frontend/src/lib/deeplink.js`: JS mirror of the Go parser, same shape and tolerances.
- `service.js` exposes `consumePendingDeepLink()` over the Wails bind. Mocked in `backend-mock.js` for standalone dev mode.
- `Root.vue` after sign-in: if `consumePendingDeepLink()` returns a user link, `router.push({ name: "Search", query: { q: id } })` instead of Home. The Search view runs `searchUsers(id)` and renders the profile — the Vue app has no per-user URL route, so this is the canonical "navigate by id" path.
- `Home.vue` on `created` + window `focus` listener: same probe, for the macOS hot-path where the app is already running and the OS dispatches the URL via `Mac.OnUrlOpen` while the user is on Home.

### What stays the same
- `OnSecondInstanceLaunch` keeps panicking — single instance by design. On Windows/Linux a `warpnet://...` click while the app is already running will (per design) trigger that panic; the user re-opens the app to continue. macOS is unaffected: it uses `Mac.OnUrlOpen` instead.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./cmd/node/member/deeplink/...` — `TestParse` (10 cases incl. whitespace-trim) asserts `Link.Raw` end-to-end; `TestFromArgs` covers the dash-stripped form.
- [x] `golangci-lint` on touched paths — 0 issues.
- [x] Cross-compile: `GOOS=linux/windows/darwin go build ./cmd/node/member/deeplink/...`.
- [x] `npm test` in `frontend/` — 94/94 (parser unit tests + new Root cases for the deep-link → Search branch and the unparseable-fallback branch).
- [ ] Manual e2e on each OS:
  - install / first-run → app registers itself for `warpnet://`
  - browser: open `warpnet://user/abc` from the address bar → confirmation dialog → app focuses, Vue routes to Search?q=abc
  - cold-start with `warpnet --warpnet://user/abc` arg → same result via `os.Args`
  - macOS only: click `warpnet://` link while app is running → `Mac.OnUrlOpen` fires, focus listener on Home picks it up, same result

author: alambertt
body:
## What & why

Two related improvements to how disabled requests behave in the editor, plus a quality-of-life toggle.

### 1. Disabling a recorded redirect follow-up no longer breaks the parent
The recorder stores `follow_redirects: false` on a request that leads to a recorded redirect step (the redirect is an explicit follow-up step rather than auto-followed). While the follow-up was enabled, the editor force-displayed the parent's **Follow Redirects** checkbox as checked-and-locked, hiding that `false`. As soon as the follow-up was disabled, the stored `false` surfaced — the box went unchecked **and** the config became broken (redirect neither auto-followed nor handled by the now-disabled step).

Fixed at the **data layer** so the downloaded YAML is correct:
- **Disable follow-up → source `follow_redirects: true`** (auto-follow; checkbox checked **and** editable, since the recorded linkage is now broken).
- **Enable follow-up → source `follow_redirects: false`** (restores recorded behavior; checkbox checked-and-locked via existing display logic).

The sync (`syncRedirectSourceFollowRedirects`) runs at **all** toggle entry points — detail-panel toggle, tree right-click, and bulk toolbar — so behavior is consistent however you disable.

### 2. A disabled request's detail form is read-only
The Request/Response panel for a disabled request still renders all fields, but inside a disabled `<fieldset>` (dimmed, non-interactive) to prevent meaningless edits. The Request/Response tab bar stays clickable so you can still browse it.

### 3. Enable/Disable toggle in the detail-panel header
An Enabled/Disabled pill toggle in the shared detail-panel header lets you flip a node without right-clicking. It appears for every node type that supports enabling (same exclusions as the context menu: `root`, `test`, `scenarios`, `steps`) and reuses the same `updateNodeEnabled` op, so it cascades to the subtree identically.

## Changes
- `types/yaml.ts` — `RedirectSourceInfo` gains `targetDisabled`.
- `YAMLEditor.tsx` — populate `targetDisabled`; new `handleToggleNodeEnabled`; pass `onToggleEnabled` to the detail panel.
- `YAMLTreeView.tsx` — apply redirect sync in context-menu and bulk toggles.
- `treeOperations.ts` — new `syncRedirectSourceFollowRedirects` helper.
- `YAMLRequestDetails.tsx` — unlock redirect checkboxes when the follow-up is disabled; wrap the form in a disabled `<fieldset>` when the request is disabled.
- `YAMLNodeDetails.tsx` — Enabled/Disabled pill toggle in the header.
- `i18n/en.ts`, `i18n/es.ts` — `enabled`/`disabled` labels.

## Reviewer notes
- **Re-enabling a follow-up resets the parent's `follow_redirects` to `false`** (the recorded value). A manual override set while the follow-up was disabled would be overwritten on re-enable — intentional, to keep the config matching the recording. Flag if you'd prefer to preserve manual overrides.
- The disabled-form `<fieldset>` covers all native controls including the plain-`<textarea>` body editor; the Monaco editor (only used for very large bodies, >2000 lines / >120 KB) ignores `fieldset disabled` and was left as-is per minimal-change scope.

## Verification
- `bun run build` ✅
- `bun run lint` ✅ (0 errors; pre-existing warnings only)
- `bun run test` ✅ (140 passed, 2 skipped)

author: kane50613
body:
`ImageNode.src` is typed `string | Uint8Array | ArrayBuffer`, but inline bytes never actually rendered — and not because of `skip_deserializing` (that's on the unrelated `Loaded` variant). The real cause: `ImageSourceInput::Buffer` was `Vec<u8>`, which deserializes via `deserialize_seq` and only accepts a JSON-style array of numbers. A real `Uint8Array`/`ArrayBuffer` crosses both the napi and WASM boundaries as a *bytes value* (`visit_bytes` / `visit_byte_buf`), so it never matched the untagged enum and deserialization failed on **both** `@takumi-rs/core` and `@takumi-rs/wasm`.

This replaces the original JS-side base64 workaround with a one-type Rust fix: `Buffer(Vec<u8>)` → `Buffer(serde_bytes::ByteBuf)`. `ByteBuf` deserializes via `deserialize_bytes`, which serde's untagged machinery satisfies from buffered `Content::Bytes`/`ByteBuf`. Inline raster and SVG bytes are decoded directly by the renderer (`ImageSource::from_bytes` sniffs the format) — no base64 round-trip, ~33% smaller payloads.

### Behaviour
- `image({ src })` accepts `Uint8Array` / `ArrayBuffer` directly; the helper passes `src` through unchanged.
- Raster bytes (invalid UTF-8) → `Buffer` variant → format-sniffed. SVG markup (valid UTF-8) → `Url` variant → existing SVG path. No JS special-casing needed.
- **Limitation:** bytes ride the native/WASM boundary as-is. A node tree explicitly serialized to JSON (e.g. posted to the HTTP server) still needs a `data:` URI string.

### Tests
- Core unit test deserializing a bytes value into `Buffer` (red on `Vec<u8>`, green on `ByteBuf`).
- napi integration: inline `Uint8Array`/`ArrayBuffer` and SVG-as-bytes render pixel-identical to the fetchedResources / string paths.
- wasm verified by mechanism (identical `Content::ByteBuf` path) + compile + clippy.

### Motivation

### Describe how you validated your changes

author: george-payne
body:
Turns three "technically correct but unhelpful" projection errors into clear messages.

- **`foreachStream()` on `fromStream()`/`fromStreams()`** (`JintProjectionHandler.cs`) - threw a raw `Property 'foreachStream' of object is not a function`. Now keeps the method reachable on those sources and throws a friendly `InvalidProjectionException` ("foreachStream() is only supported with fromAll() and fromCategory()"), mirroring the `$deleted` rejection.
- **Duplicate `options()`** (`DiagnosticCollector.cs`) - was silently last-write-wins. New `options.duplicate` compile-time warning on each call past the first (surfaced in the editor via LSP).
- **Malformed fed events** (`testing/js/src/schemas.ts`) - `parseEventInput` ran a union schema, giving valibot's cryptic `Expected Object but received Object`. Now discriminates on the shape key (`eventType`/`event`/`type`) and parses the specific schema, so the error names the bad field, with a friendly fallback for an unrecognized shape.
- **Changeset** - patch for `@kurrent/gaffer-runtime`, `@kurrent/gaffer`, `@kurrent/projections-testing`.

author: porteightyeighty
body:
Strengthens AstBuilder validation and fills gaps in AST test coverage.

  Fixes
  - Variable references and assignments were entirely broken: PATHSEP() returns a list (never null), so the guard rejected every simple path. Now correctly accepts single-segment paths and rejects only multi-segment/generic ones.
  - Let bindings now require an explicit type (clean UnsupportedConstructException instead of an NPE on let x = 0;).
  - Corrected the misleading message on the untyped-parameter guard.

  Tests
  - New AssignmentBuilderTest: assignment to a variable, and rejection of field/deref/index targets.
  - ExpressionBuilderTest: variable expressions; rejection of multi-segment and turbofish paths.
  - StatementBuilderTest: let mut; rejection of ;, nested items, and macros.
  - ItemBuilderTest: multi-param functions; rejection of non-function items and varargs.
  - CrateBuilderTest: multiple functions in one crate.

author: roblillack
body:
This PR includes massive performance improvements for rendering drop shadows, especially on HiDPI displays:

* We're using improved damage detection, to reduce the number of bytes updated when changing the style on focus change (no need to copy window content around)
* We stop clearing the buffers after creation ;)
* We precalulate the shadow parts needed (corners, sides) and only multiply them onto the surfaces instead of calculating each individual pixel each time (parts are cached & shared between windows)
* Size buffer for the larger of the active/inactive sizes so we do not need to reallocate when focus changes
* Added rendering instrumentation behind `--features debug-logging`

In total this is a 10x improvement of the time taken when switching a window from inactive to active when drop shadows are enabled. On my machine: >200ms in dev mode to ~20ms; <10ms consistently in release mode.

author: realryannichols
body:
## Summary
Drafts can't be viewed at their public `/posts/[slug]` URL (RLS + the published-only query), and the admin preview is login-gated — so there was no way to share an **unpublished** draft with an outside reviewer (a source, a family) for sign-off before publishing.

This adds **`/preview/post/[id]`**: a `force-dynamic`, `robots: noindex` page that reads a single post by UUID via the service client and renders it with `PostMain`. The UUID is the secret — the page is never linked from the site and is not indexed, so only someone with the exact link can open it.

## Notes
- Anyone with the link can read that one post; it cannot enumerate others (single `.eq("id", uuid)` lookup, UUIDv4 is unguessable). A banner on the page tells reviewers not to share the link publicly.
- No change to the public feed, the `/posts/[slug]` route, or RLS.

author: sclfnc
body:
Extended Vue 3 + D3 dashboard and a new FastAPI backend. **Additive** — `assets/`, `docs/`, the group README and the existing frontend are preserved.

It's a substantial rewrite, but with no breaking changes — the existing API contract is fully preserved.

> **Diff size = file count, not removed work.**

## Frontend (`frontend/`) — extended

> Not the final version yet: minor fixes and enhancements are still planned. Core algorithms and functionality won't change.

Guide mode driven by a panel registry. Implemented panels:

- **Descriptive** — Degree Distribution (PMF/CCDF, by-type, 4 fits: power-law/exponential/log-normal/ Poisson), Connected Components (WCC/SCC, bubbles/bars, drill-down by type)
- **Centrality** — PageRank, Eigenvector, Betweenness, Closeness (parametric panel) + 4×4 Comparison scatter matrix
- **Local** — Ego Network (k-hop, direction), Ego Comparison (up to 4 egos, union/intersection)
- **Mixing** — Type Mixing Matrix (Newman assortativity), Edge Flow (radial meta-graph)
- **Temporal** — Activity Timeline (node + edge scope), brush writes a temporal filter

Cross-panel model:

- 3 shared bitmaps (`activeNodeMask`, `activeEdgeMask`, `selectedMask`) built once
- **mask-only**: filters attenuate marks, never recompute metrics (fits/curves stay full-graph)
- per-panel Isolation (Lock); left sidebar filter editor (type chips, ranges, per-attribute constraints)

Removed: default Vite scaffold only (`HelloWorld.vue`, `TheWelcome.vue`, demo icons, `counter.js`,
`AboutView.vue`) — generator boilerplate, not group work.

## Backend (`api/`) — new

- **Stateless**: serves full topology (columnar SoA) + precomputed indices; client builds bitmasks
- filtering/selection are client-side vector/bitwise ops → **0 network round-trips**
- payloads small: ≈6 MB MC1 source → a few hundred KB of typed arrays
- ~20 single-responsibility modules;

Endpoints:

- **Data** — `/schema/`, `/nodes/`, `/edges/`, `/metrics/`, `/degree-fit/`, `/components/`,
  `/attribute-index/`, `/effective-types/`, `/type-mixing/`, `/edge-flow/`, `/timeline/`, `/ego/`,
  `/node-inspect/`, `/edge-inspect/`
- **Centrality** — async precompute + polling: `/centrality-status/`, `/centrality/{spectral,
  betweenness,closeness}/`
- **Datasets** — `/datasets/`, `/datasets/load/{name}`, `/upload/`, `/health/`

Built-ins: 4 generated by NetworkX, 2 (email-eu, MovieLens) fetched on first use from official hosts
(URLs + licences in `api/builtin_download.py`). None committed.

## Compatibility

- legacy endpoints (`/summary/`, `/node-types/`, `/edge-types/`, `/set-default/` + `default_graph_id`)
  preserved verbatim in `legacy_compat.py`, isolated; modular layer never imports it
- `/upload/`, `/health/` shared → supersets, same response shape
- upstream `tests/` vendored unchanged; only `conftest.py` adds a fixture seeding a synthetic
  `default-graph.json` (MC1 not redistributable) → **72 passed offline**

## Docs

Each folder is documented; start from the one matching what you're reviewing.

- **[`README.md`](README.md)** — group README, intact (+ Repository Status pointer, Team line)
- **[`README.sclfnc.md`](README.sclfnc.md)** — Telescope reference implementation: design, panels,
  cross-panel model, stack, scope & limitations
- **[`contract.md`](contract.md)** — the cross-panel interaction contract (bitmap-truth, mask-only,
  effective-types, Lock, upstream-write policy)
- **[`api/README.md`](api/README.md)** — self-contained **backend manual**: design model, module map,
  dependency DAG, every endpoint, how to extend without breaking compatibility, testing
- **[`api/tests/README.md`](api/tests/README.md)** — test suite layout: fixtures, legacy vs modular
  suites, the `seed_default_graph` fixture
- **[`frontend/README.md`](frontend/README.md)** — frontend setup; **[`frontend/src/panels/README.md`](frontend/src/panels/README.md)** — D3 panel system
- **`assets/`, `docs/`** — group meeting material, unchanged

💡 Vulnerabilidade: O endpoint de `/api/login` possuía uma implementação customizada, em memória, para realizar o rate limiting. Esta implementação não era escalável para uso distribuído, propensa a bugs de concorrência e não seguia a mesma padronização de segurança (Flask-Limiter) adotada no resto da aplicação para defesa em profundidade.

author: trex0092
body:
## Root cause (finally identified)

The persistent `Build script returned non-zero exit code: 2` was **memory over-allocation**, not the fd/EMFILE/lockfile/TypeScript issues chased in PRs #687–#692.

**Proof the build is not broken:** the full `scripts/build.sh` runs to **exit 0 locally under the same `ulimit -n 4096`** as the Netlify build agent — all 6 steps green, in-build TypeScript passed (113s), 133 static pages generated, build traces collected, webpack compile in 2.7 min. Same commit, same fd limit, opposite outcome → the failure is **environmental**.

**The mechanism:** `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192` tells V8 it may grow its heap to 8 GB. On a Netlify build container without 8 GB free per process, V8 defers garbage collection until 8 GB, so the kernel OOM-kills `next build` *before* GC runs. Netlify surfaces that as the generic **exit code 2** (no JS heap-OOM stack trace). The earlier bump to 8192 didn't fix the failure — **it caused it.**

## Fix

Lower the heap cap to **4096** (Netlify's documented safe default) in both places it is set:
- `netlify.toml` `[build.environment]` (applies to steps 1–5 + the plugin)
- the step-6 `NODE_OPTIONS` override in `scripts/build.sh`

4 GB clears the original ~1.5 GB default OOM while leaving the container headroom for the OS, webpack workers, and `@netlify/plugin-nextjs`. The local build proves <4 GB is sufficient.

## Verification
- ✅ `bash scripts/build.sh` → exit 0 locally (ulimit -n 4096)
- ✅ `tsc --noEmit` root → exit 0
- ✅ all 133 pages generated, traces collected, no EMFILE

author: aybook
body:
Part of #294 (HBRI audit follow-ups), Tier-1.

## Problem

The HBRI side-channel port was `tcp_ports[1] or ssl_ports[1]` (plain, falling back to TLS), and `hbri_dual_stack` counted a TLS-only family as dual-stack. The hub then advertised a TLS port in the plain-text `ITCP`; the client opened a PLAIN side-channel to a TLS listener, the handshake produced no `HTCP`, and HBRI silently timed out on every attempt for that family. Fail-safe (secondary stayed stripped) but a silent misconfiguration trap, and it contradicted the `active()` / `cfg_defaults` comments that already require a "plain listener on BOTH families".

## Fix

Drop the TLS fallback - the side-channel port is the first PLAIN port for the family only. A family without a plain listener leaves the port nil -> `hbri_dual_stack` false -> `active()` false -> HBRI not advertised / not solicited (the secure default), instead of advertised-but-broken. Code now matches the existing comments.

## Tests

New `tests/unit/hbri_test.lua` (the module had no unit test): locks the `active()` activation gate - in particular "no plain port on a family -> `active()` false", the contract this fix relies on - plus the `eligible()` contract (placeholder discovery #291, opposite-family requirement, ADHBRI gate). Wired into both CI lua steps (Linux lua5.4 + Windows msys2 lua). 15 checks.

Smoke (plain listeners on both families): all HBRI tests still green - the plain-both-families path is unchanged.

Note: a dedicated smoke test for the TLS-only-family case would need a second hub instance with a TLS-only family (the harness runs a single shared hub), which is disproportionate for a fail-safe fallback removal; the unit test locks the consumer-side gate instead.

body:
## Sprint O4 — Batched-Bucketed JAX GPU (destrava o gargalo on-the-fly)

Faz `simulate_multi_jax_batched` usar o kernel **bucketed** quando a geometria é
compartilhada entre os modelos do batch (regime PINN / geração on-the-fly), em vez
do `unified` hardcodado (~6.9× mais lento). Reusa `_get_bucket_jit` + `jax.vmap`
sobre o eixo de modelos.

### Ganho de performance (A6000 48 GB, c128)
| Regime | Antes (batched-unified) | Depois (batched-bucketed) | Ganho |
|:-------|:-----------------------:|:-------------------------:|:-----:|
| On-the-fly 32 modelos × 600 pos | 65.1k mod/h | **1.466M mod/h** | **22.5×** |
| Cenário H (8×8×8 = 512 cfg) | OOM ~110 GB | roda c/ `chunk_size_models=8` | destrava |

> Supera Numba 4w×16t (~1.05M) no regime batched. (Single-model pequeno: Numba ainda vence — esperado.)

### Mudanças
- **batched-bucketed** + dispatcher por geometria homogênea (`np.allclose atol=0`) + fallback `unified` (warning).
- **`SimulationConfig.jax_chunk_size_models`** — fatia o eixo de modelos (fix OOM Cenário H).
- **Fix bug latente `_CTX_CACHE`**: colisão de chave n=1↔n=2 (esp vazio em ambos) → `_hash_ctx_key` inclui `n`.
- Bench: defaults bucketed + `--chunk-size-models` + Cenário H habilitado.

### Validação
- **Gates F1–F4: 220 PASS / 0 FAIL** — paridade Fortran c128 **<1e-12 inviolável preservada**.
- Paridade O4 **<1e-13**: batched-bucketed vs serial bucketed (n=3/5/10) / vs batched-unified / multi-dim 3TR×3dip×2f; chunking bit-exato (bucketed).
- Review multi-agente: physics **PASS**, code **PASS**, adversarial **CONCERNS** (1 P1 — portabilidade CPU do teste de chunk — resolvido; P2s documentados).

Relatório: `docs/reports/v2.44_sprint_O4_batched_bucketed_2026-05-29.md`

body:
## 背景

排查「你进入了 门户 节点」这条 system reminder 是否存在一次性重复追加的风险时确认：`consumeIncomingEventInActiveState` 在每个非焦点子状态变化时都会 push 一条 `createStateReminderMessage(focusedStateId)`。`consumePendingEvents` / `hydrateStartupEvents` 按事件逐条循环消费，攒进 `pendingIncomingMessages` 后一次性 append——焦点停在门户时，同批 N 条群/私聊消息会向上下文重复灌入 N 条逐字相同的门户 reminder，既污染上下文又破坏 KV 缓存前缀（启动补水场景尤其严重）。

## 改动

- 移除 `consumeIncomingEventInActiveState` 中的焦点 reminder 刷新块（`needsReminderRefresh` 判断 + 重复 push）。非焦点子状态变化不再追加任何 reminder。
- 删除随之变成死代码的私有方法 `hasDescendantState`。
- `shouldTriggerRound` 不再被重新赋值，改为 `const`。
- 跨状态通知（`notificationAccumulator`）逻辑保持不变。

## 行为变化

焦点停在门户时，后台群/私聊消息不再触发轮次（消息仍照常累积进各状态 unread，下次 `enter` 时可见）。

## 验证

- `tsc --noEmit` 通过；ESLint、Prettier 通过。
- 相关测试全过：`root-agent-session`、`enter.tool`、`back.tool`、`notification-accumulator`。其中一条断言旧刷新行为的用例已改写为新行为的回归保护。

body:
## Resumen

Implementa el **backend** del catálogo de instrumentos por curso (Fase 2 del plan), base del futuro motor de incertidumbres. Gestionable por docentes, con export/import para reutilizarlo entre cursos/años.

Se divide en commits chicos:

1. **Esquema** — tablas `instruments` e `instrument_scales` (con `b_model` = `resolucion`/`apreciacion`/`fabricante`, specs de fabricante `pct`/`coef`/`fijo`, y `internal_res`/`internal_res_u`), structs `Instrument`/`InstrumentScale` documentados.
2. **Capa de datos** (`src/instruments.rs`) — CRUD por curso (instrumentos y escalas) y export/import del catálogo entre cursos.
3. **API REST** — endpoints bajo `/api/instruments` (listar/crear/editar/borrar + escalas + export/import), todos bajo `require_teacher`.
4. **Seed** — catálogo inicial real: regla, calibre, cronómetro (R=0.001 s), balanza, testers A830L y EXTECH MN35 (con specs de fabricante y resistencia interna) y osciloscopio GDS-1052-U en voltaje (3%·V + 0.1·V/div + 1mV) y tiempo (1% de la medida).

## Modelo de incertidumbre tipo B por escala

- `resolucion` (digital simple): `u_B = step / (2√3)`
- `apreciacion` (analógico): `u_B = appreciation / √6`
- `fabricante` (tester/osciloscopio): `U = pct·|v| + coef·step + fijo`, `u_B = U/2`

Contrastado con las técnicas de trabajo vigentes (Estadística, CC, RC, Alterna).

## Tests

- 52 tests (unit + integración con base SQLite temporal) + 8 doctests, todos en verde, sin warnings.
- Cobertura del catálogo: CRUD, posiciones, borrado de escalas, roundtrip de export/import, seed idempotente, y validadores de la API.
- Verificado end-to-end: `GET /api/instruments?course_id=...` devuelve los instrumentos sembrados con sus escalas.

## Pendiente (PR aparte)

- Frontend: pestaña **Instrumentos** (CRUD + exportar/importar).

`TsDateField` / `TsDateTimeField` gain `disableFuture`, `maxDate`, `minDate`. Out-of-range days are disabled in the calendar and rejected on manual text entry (today stays selectable with `disableFuture`).

### ts-form — button: icon support
`TsButtonField` gains `icon` (Lucide name) and `iconOnly`, so a button field can render as a compact icon button (e.g. a currency-swap `< >` control).

### ts-table — open import pipeline
New `onImportFile(file: File)` prop. When set, the raw selected file is handed to the consumer and the built-in XLSX parsing + column filtering is skipped, so imports can be parsed correctly (UTF-8, cells kept as strings, all columns preserved). Falls back to the existing `onImport` when not set.

### ts-table — view-state persistence
New `persistStateKey` prop persists sorting, column filters, column visibility/order/sizing, global filter and pagination to `localStorage` and restores them on mount — so settings survive navigating to a detail page and back. New `ts-table/persistence.ts` helper is registered in the registry entry.

### Tests
Added: persistence round-trip unit tests, an `onImportFile` raw-file test, and a state-restoration test. `biome ci` and `vitest run --coverage` pass locally.

author: zy-wang-0304
body:
## 背景 / 目标

引入分组功能后，分组 foreground 挂载在 `.canvas-shell` 根层；画布放大时组框的实际 DOM 尺寸会扩大外层 document / Webview scroll area，导致无限画布出现整体横向或纵向滚动条。本 MR 修复该问题：画布整体仍只通过 pan / zoom 导航，不出现外层滚动条。

后续复测发现，foreground 改挂到 React Flow renderer 后，分组拖拽事件会继续被 React Flow pane 识别为画布 pan，造成拖动分组时画板也参与移动、视觉上出现不规则偏移。本 MR 也一并修复这条回归。

## 主要改动

- 将分组可交互 foreground portal 从 `.canvas-shell` 改为 React Flow `.react-flow__renderer`，让分组标题、边框、toolbar 和 resize 控制点与 React Flow pane 共用裁切边界。
- 为 React Flow wrapper / renderer / pane 明确设置 `overflow: hidden`，避免放大后的分组 DOM 扩大 Webview scroll area。
- 给分组 foreground frame 增加 `nodrag nopan`，避免分组拖动被 React Flow pane 同时解释为画布平移。
- 新增 Playwright 回归：在 640x520 viewport、1.8x zoom 下渲染大分组，断言 document / shell scroll 尺寸不超过 client 尺寸，并确认分组 foreground 与 pane 同处 renderer 层。
- 新增 Playwright 回归：在 1.8x zoom 下拖动分组，断言分组草稿跟随鼠标位移、viewport transform 不变，并最终发出正确 `webview/moveGroup` 位置。
- 同步更新 `docs/design-docs/canvas-node-groups.md`，记录分组 foreground / background 的挂载层级与无限画布不出现整体滚动条的不变量。

## 验证方式

- `npm run typecheck` 通过。
- `npm run test:canvas-node-groups` 通过。
- `node scripts/test/run-playwright-webview.mjs --grep "canvas groups render|canvas groups do not create document scrollbars|canvas group drag follows|canvas group body|canvas groups resize|canvas group border stroke|canvas group title and action"` 通过，10 条 Webview 分组相关用例通过。

## 残余风险

- 本轮覆盖 Webview harness 中的滚动条和分组拖拽回归；未额外执行完整 `npm run test` 和 VSCode smoke。

body: ## Summary - Fix Azure Search indexing to derive document keys from the user-scoped blob path instead of the caller-provided resource ID. - Add a regression test showing two users' onboarding blob paths produce distinct document IDs. ## Bug and Impact User-scoped generated files such as onboarding markdown and goals markdown used global resource IDs like `onboarding.md` and `goals`. Azure Search upserts by `id`, so one user's indexing run could overwrite another user's document in the shared index, causing RAG context loss and significant cross-tenant search breakage. ## Root Cause `AzureSearchClient` built the search key from `resourceId`, but several callers pass non-tenant-scoped resource IDs for generated user context documents. ## Fix Use `blobPath`, which already includes the user-scoped storage location, when building the Azure Search document ID. ## Validation - Attempted `dotnet test ProjectBrain.Api.Tests/ProjectBrain.Api.Tests.csproj`, but the cloud image does not have the .NET SDK installed (`dotnet: command not found`).

author: sergiocorral-conductorone
body:
## Problem

The `main ci` workflow ([main.yaml]) fails on every push to `main` with an opaque `exit code 1` ([run 26653029538](https://github.com/ConductorOne/baton-twingate/actions/runs/26653029538/job/78557609363)). It runs `go test -v -covermode=count -json ./... > test.json`, so the real error is redirected into `test.json` and never appears in the log.

## Root cause

`main.yaml` is a stale, redundant workflow:
- It duplicates **lint + test**, which the baton-admin-managed shared `verify.yaml` already runs on push and PR (and that run passes ✓).
- It pins Go `1.23.x` via `setup-go@v4` while `go.mod` requires `go 1.25.2`, forcing a runtime toolchain download (`go: downloading go1.25.2`) — a fragile flow that fails in CI but not via the shared workflow.
- It uses deprecated action versions (`checkout@v3`, `setup-go@v4`, Node 20) and even runs `Install Go` before `Checkout`.

The repo already moved lint/test to `verify.yaml` (see `ee03228 chore: remove ci.yaml (lint and test handled by verify.yaml)`); `main.yaml` is a leftover that should have been removed at the same time.

## Fix

Delete `main.yaml`. Coverage is unchanged:
- `verify.yaml` → lint + test (shared `@v4`)
- `ci.yaml` → integration sync-test (role grant/revoke)

author: leoromanovsky
body:
## Motivation

Feature Flags server SDK documentation did not explain how serverless workloads receive Remote Configuration payloads. Users running on AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Run, Azure Functions, and similar platforms need clear guidance that the Datadog Agent is the supported path for server-side flag payload delivery today, and that deeper serverless support is planned for a future release.

## Changes

This PR adds a new Serverless Environments guide under the Feature Flags Implementation Patterns folder. The guide explains the Agent-backed Remote Configuration flow, required environment variables, operational considerations, local evaluation, public API limitations, and validation steps.

It also adds environment-specific notes for AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Run services and functions, Azure Functions, AWS Fargate/container tasks, and managed edge/function platforms. The wording now avoids claiming unverified external-Agent connectivity as confirmed support; it tells users to validate an Agent-backed architecture in a non-production environment before relying on it for feature flag delivery.

The PR adds the Implementation Patterns folder to the Feature Flags left navigation and keeps the server SDK overview linked to the serverless guidance through both inline copy and further reading. It also clarifies that `DD_REMOTE_CONFIGURATION_ENABLED` is the Agent Remote Configuration setting, while `DD_REMOTE_CONFIG_ENABLED` is a tracer-side setting used by some SDKs.

## Decisions

The guidance stays high level and architecture-focused instead of duplicating language-specific SDK setup. The page explicitly calls out that the public Feature Flags API is for management, not per-request flag evaluation, and that application-owned defaults or static configuration are outside Remote Configuration delivery when no Agent path is available.

The document uses validate-first wording for external Agent patterns, especially for Cloud Run, until those specific deployment models are confirmed separately.

- YAML/front matter parse for changed Feature Flags pages and `config/_default/menus/main.en.yaml`

## Summary
- Adds a zero-voting-power guard to the Member Vote close-and-tally handler before any on-chain `active` update is prepared or sent.
- Returns `503` when real, non-snapshot vote rows exist but the resolved tally has `totalParticipationVP === 0`, which strongly indicates failed vMOONEY reads rather than a legitimate result.
- Excludes snapshot sentinel rows from the real-vote count so re-tally behavior remains compatible.

## Why
`fetchTotalVMOONEYs` catches chain/Engine read failures and returns an all-zero array. Without this guard, `nonProjectVote.ts` can compute `passed = false` and write `PROJECT_VOTE_FAILED` on-chain for a proposal that actually passed.

body: ## Contexto Feedback de sessão real após #60: o /start deve **entregar o Cérebro preenchido** (não em branco), trazer o usuário ao **Companion com permissão**, e terminar com um **projeto pronto para uso** + menu do que dá pra fazer. ## Mudanças **1. Escrita direta no Cérebro (escopo ONBOARDING)** — decisão do Diego: relaxar a regra "nada vira contexto sem aprovação" no onboarding, trocando por **autorização prévia** (o Passo 0 já pergunta). Registra **uma** entrada `type: decision` com `approver = usuário` e `evidence = URLs + info adicional`. - **Escopo preservado**: os demais gates (DataForSEO, source separation, `approve-cluster` para novas subpáginas de cluster) e o `brain-keeper` (edições fora do onboarding) **permanecem intactos**. author: max33verstappenf1
body:
## Description

Bug fix: the monolithic `vertex-simple` proxy (`Google/apigee/apiproxy/`) fails to deploy on Apigee X.

`SC-AIRSScan` and `SC-AIRSResponseScan` set the AIRS target URL to `{private.prisma.airs.url}/v1/scan/sync/request` — a URL that **begins with a variable**. Apigee statically validates target URLs at deploy time and rejects it:

```
messaging.adaptors.http.configuration.MalformedTargetUrl:
"Invalid/Malformed URL {private.prisma.airs.url}/v1/scan/sync/request provided for target SC-AIRSScan"
```

The deployed revision goes to `state: ERROR` and the proxy returns `404 ApplicationNotFound` at runtime.

## Fix

Split the scheme out so the URL begins with a literal `https://`, and store the **host** in the KVM:

- `SC-AIRSScan` / `SC-AIRSResponseScan`: `<URL>https://{private.prisma.airs.host}/v1/scan/sync/request</URL>`
- `KVM-GetConfig`: read `prisma.airs.host` → `private.prisma.airs.host`

The AIRS region stays configurable (set the host per tenant region).

## Config contract change

Set the KVM key **`prisma.airs.host`** to the AIRS endpoint **host only** (e.g. `service.api.aisecurity.paloaltonetworks.com`), not a full URL. (Previously `prisma.airs.url` held a full URL — which is exactly what triggered the malformed-URL rejection.)

## Docs alignment (`README.md` / `ARCHITECTURE.md`)

While here, corrected the KVM listings in the `Google/apigee/` docs, which had drifted from the actual `<Parameter>` values in `KVM-GetConfig.xml`:

- `airs.token` → `prisma.airs.token`, `airs.profile` → `prisma.airs.profile`.
- Added the `prisma.airs.host` entry — it was never listed even though the ServiceCallout has always read it. Documented setting it to a regional host (US / EU) instead of editing the bundle.
- Fixed the UI underscore-key example (`airs_token` → `prisma_airs_token`).

(The block-response section in this README is unchanged: the monolith genuinely returns **HTTP 400** via `RF-Block` — that's correct, and distinct from the SharedFlow's graceful-200 envelope corrected in #42.)

## How Has This Been Tested?

Deployed `vertex-simple` on a live Apigee X evaluation org:
- Before: revision `state: ERROR` (MalformedTargetUrl), `/vertex` → `404`.
- After: revision deploys READY; `/vertex` benign prompt → `200`, prompt-injection → blocked by `RF-Block`.

## Types of changes

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking code; minor config-key change documented above)
- [x] Documentation update (KVM key-name accuracy)

## Checklist

- [x] No real credentials in the diff.
- [x] Conventional commit messages.
- [x] Verified deploying on a clean Apigee X org.

author: tomgr
body:
The HTTP fetcher read each download fully into memory (io.ReadAll) before storing it in the CAS, so large numbers of parallel fetches could cause OOMs.

Two changes address this:
- When the blob's digest is known up front (a checksum.sri using the request's digest function, plus a Content-Length), the response is streamed straight to the CAS without being buffered at all.
- Otherwise the body has to be read to compute the digest. This is still buffered in memory by default, but the new download_directory_path option buffers it in a temporary file on disk instead.

This was written with Claude but I've carefully reviewed it all and tested it end to end locally.

author: nibsbin
body:
## Summary

Stamps the PDF `/Info` `/Producer` string on every Typst-rendered PDF (`Quillmark <version>` by default, overridable via render options), and folds it together with the existing signature-field AcroForm injection into a **single** incremental-update pass.

`typst_pdf` leaves `/Producer` unset (it only writes `/Creator`), so this fills the apt standard field. Consumers can override it via `RenderOptions.producer`, threaded through the core, WASM, and Python render APIs.

## Key changes

- **Unified `overlay` pass** (`crates/backends/typst/src/overlay/`): one incremental update carries both the `/Info` `/Producer` rewrite (preserving Typst's `/Creator`) and, when present, the signature widgets + `/AcroForm`. One appended xref/trailer, one `/Prev` link; `/Info` and `/ID` are forwarded exactly once. Object ids come from a single counter so a fresh `/Info` can't collide with widget ids.
- **Shared `pdf_scan` module**: the byte-level scanner (lifted from `sig_overlay/scanner`) plus a reusable `append_incremental_update` writer used by the pass.
- **`RenderOptions.producer`** added to core, WASM, and Python bindings.
- **PDF text-string encoding** for the producer: ASCII literal (with `()`/`\` escaping) or UTF-16BE+BOM hex for non-ASCII overrides. Dictionary splicing derives key spans from `find_dict_value`'s slice (no fragile re-scan).
- **Examples**: render examples now use `blueprint_filled(FillBehavior::Preview)` so they render out of the box after the upstream blueprint-fill change.
- **Fixtures**: `usaf_memo` 0.2.0 plate now injects an empty `signature-field` above the signature block (the bundled template's `query(metadata).last()` was hardened to `.first()` so the field's metadata doesn't shadow its config); the redundant `usaf_memo` 0.1.0 fixture was removed and all references repointed to 0.2.0.
- **Docs**: `signature-field` doc + format-designer guide note that it emits a document-global `metadata` element.

## Tests

- `producer_meta.rs`: default producer, override (incl. literal-string escaping and a non-ASCII UTF-16BE round-trip), `/Creator` preservation, and composition with a signature field.
- Existing signature-field acceptance tests and the quiver render-all test exercise the unified pass.

##### New Async and Deferred mechanism

Instead of using async.js and defer.js, your executable config files can return a synchronous or asynchronous function. Note that if you use async deferred functions through the new mechanism, **you need to call Util.resolveAsyncConfig()** instead of the old version.

`Util.resolveAsyncConfig()` also fixes an issue where using defer in an array did not function properly [#​876](https://redirect.github.com/node-config/node-config/issues/876)

The old implementations have been marked as deprecated and will issue warnings to console.error to indicate use of the old pathways. The old functions are incompatible with ESM loading conventions and will be removed at the beginning of the 5.0 cycle to facilitate conversion of the library to ESM.

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/node-config/node-config/compare/v4.0.1...v4.1.0)

##### Breaking Changes

Several bugs were fixed that a user code might theoretically rely on, but most likely not:

- Config.getSources() no longer contains files read by parseFile outside of the load process
- when `setModuleDefaults('modulename', ...)` is called twice, the second call can overwrite values from the first
- Config.getSources() now agrees with `setModuleDefaults`, no matter how often it is called

##### What's Changed

**Updated Note**: A number of functions in config.util have been marked as deprecated. The consensus among the maintainers is that these create a substantial surface area that should not have been exposed in this manner. This however has mostly been mentioned in bug responses and in the Discussion forums but previously not announced in the documentation.

These functions have been by and large moved into lib/util.js, for accelerated deletion. This is all part of a fairly large raft of work
intented to move node-config to be an ESM module. Please refer to the 4.x and 5.0 [milestones](https://redirect.github.com/node-config/node-config/milestones) for additional clarification.

Bugs fixed:

- [#​687](https://redirect.github.com/node-config/node-config/issues/687) - you can now have deferConfig lines in submodules

## Problem

`EvaluationResult.feedback_config` silently drops unknown or partial dict fields. When a user passes `{"custom_key": "value"}` to `feedback_config`, the data is discarded without error or warning, despite the type hint accepting `dict`.

The root cause is in the langsmith package: older versions used `Optional[Union[FeedbackConfig, dict]]` where Pydantic's TypedDict validation would silently strip unknown keys. This has been fixed in langsmith-sdk PR #2718 by changing the type to `Optional[dict]`.

## What this PR adds

Regression tests to ensure `EvaluationResult.feedback_config` correctly preserves dict data, including:

- Unknown/custom dict keys
- Mixed known + unknown keys
- Empty dicts
- `None` default behavior
- Nested dict structures

These tests validate the fix from langsmith-sdk and prevent future regressions in langchain_core's usage of `EvaluationResult`.

## Tests

5 new unit tests in `libs/core/tests/unit_tests/test_evaluation_feedback_config.py`, all passing.

## Revision write-workflow — PR 1/3 (create + submit)

Первый слой ручного потока **листов актуализации** (фундамент под AI bulk-revision).

### Зачем (находка)
Доменная сущность `Revision` + sub-FSM (`Submit/Approve/Reject`) + persistence (`work_program_revisions`) + GET-проекция **уже существовали**, но **не было ни одного usecase/эндпоинта** для создания/отправки/одобрения ревизии — sub-FSM был **dead-code** (как `MarkNeedsRevision()` до v0.195). Этот PR строит первый слой; approve/reject → PR 2 (v0.198.0); HTTP+DI → PR 3 (v0.199.0).

- **domain**: sentinel `ErrRevisionNotFound`; root-метод `WorkProgram.SubmitRevision(revisionID)` + хелпер `findRevision` (общий для будущих approve/reject) — медиирует переход через корень агрегата, оставляя `Revision` инкапсулированным.

- **Root-mediated переходы** (`wp.SubmitRevision`), не прямая мутация inner-сущности через `Revisions()` (он отдаёт защитную копию) — корректный DDD.

author: christophergeyer
body:
## What

A new default-true filter `filters.ignore_library_caches` that drops reads and writes under a curated set of per-library user-cache subdirectories.

## Motivation

The original end-to-end nanochat run (DAG `ef174b91...`) registered **604 artifact relations on 8 jobs, of which ~99.7 % were transient HF / library cache files** — chunk-cache binaries, dataset_info.json metadata, blob storage. They clutter the DAG and bury the real model checkpoint among them.

We considered `ignore_hf_cache` as a single-library filter but rejected it as too specialized — there are many libraries with the same per-library-cache pattern (HF, pip, uv, poetry, wandb, mlflow, pre-commit, …). A curated list is the right abstraction; HF is just one entry.

## What's included in `LIBRARY_CACHE_PATTERNS`

`/.cache/{huggingface, pip, uv, poetry, pypoetry, conda, wandb, mlflow, pre-commit, black, mypy, ruff, pylint, yarn, npm, Cypress, torch, triton, jupyter, matplotlib}/`

Matched as a substring so any home-dir variant (`/home/<user>/.cache/<lib>/`, `/root/.cache/<lib>/`, etc.) is caught without enumerating every layout.

## What stays tracked

Project-specific cache subdirs not on the curated list — e.g. `~/.cache/nanochat/` where nanochat writes its tokenizer + base/SFT checkpoints. The `test_filter_files_keeps_project_specific_cache_under_dot_cache` test locks that property in.

## Pipeline placement

Same point in the pipeline as the existing `ignore_torch_cache` / `ignore_system_reads` checks — reconstitution-time, before artifact-list construction. The tracer still captures every syscall; this filter only affects what becomes a registered artifact. **Already-registered cache artifacts on existing glaas DAGs stay until those runs are re-registered.**

## Tests

- 4 new tests in `tests/unit/test_file_filter.py`:
  - HF cache (dataset_info.json + hub blob + xet chunk) dropped when enabled.
  - HF cache kept when filter explicitly disabled (override).
  - Project-specific `~/.cache/nanochat/` paths preserved.
  - Other curated entries (pip/uv/wandb/mlflow/poetry) dropped.
- All 12 file-filter tests pass; the broader filter/provenance/config suite passes (one unrelated pre-existing telemetry failure on main not caused by this change).

## Touches

- `roar/execution/provenance/file_filter.py` — `LIBRARY_CACHE_PATTERNS`, `_is_library_cache`, category, read+write wiring.
- `roar/core/models/provenance.py` — add `library_caches` to `FilterCounts` + `total`.
- `roar/integrations/config/schema.py` — add `ignore_library_caches: bool = True`.
- `roar/integrations/config/access.py` — config-key descriptor.
- `roar/backends/ray/collector.py` — thread the flag through ray's parallel filter call site.
- `roar/cli/commands/init.py` — default `.roarconfig` template gets the new key.

author: karlmcb
body:
## What changed

In `\rk@docompound`, two improvements to Group 7 compound word diagrams:

### 1. Conjunction label beside the dashed bar (not on it)
The conjunction text (`and`, `or`, `but not`, etc.) is now rendered as a separate `\node` positioned to the **side** of the dashed vertical bar, on the face closest to the slant convergence point:
- `l` direction (verb/obj, convergence left): label placed to the **left** of the bar — `anchor=south` on the rotated node
- `r` direction (subject, convergence right): label placed to the **right** of the bar — `anchor=north` on the rotated node

### 2. Dynamic vertical separation between compound words
`csep` (the half-gap between the two word platforms) previously always equalled `rk@ht` (line height). It now also accounts for the measured width of the conjunction text:

```
csep = max(rk@ht, conj_width/2 + 4pt)
```

This means multi-word conjunctions like "but not" automatically push the platforms further apart so the rotated label fits neatly inside the bar height.

## How to review

Open `rk-test.pdf` and look at **Test 0.20** ("He painted the wall but not the ceiling") — the "but not" label should now appear to the left of the dashed bar with the platforms spaced proportionally.

author: koriyoshi2041
body:
The JIRA and LaTeX serializers decide whether a cell is empty with a plain truthiness test:

```python
# _jira.py
delimiter.join([str(item) if item else " " for item in row])
# _latex.py
new_row = [cls._escape_tex_reserved_symbols(str(item)) if item else "" for item in row]
```

So `0`, `0.0`, and `False` — all valid data — are treated as missing and exported as blank cells, silently losing data. For example `tablib.Dataset([0, False, "c"]).jira` produced `| | |c|` instead of `|0|False|c|`.

The HTML format already does this correctly with `str(item) if item is not None else ""`, so "blank only for missing values" is the intended contract. This changes both serializers to test `item not in (None, "")`, which keeps the existing `None`/empty-string behaviour (still rendered blank) while preserving real falsy values.

Added `test_jira_export_falsy_values` and `test_latex_export_falsy_values`; the existing `*_none_*` tests still pass. `pytest -k "jira or latex"` is green (12 passed).

author: rayers
body:
## Problem

`gbrain code-def <symbol>` returns **0 results for methods, constructors, fields, C structs, and Swift protocols** — i.e. most of the symbols in an object-oriented codebase. `code-def <class>` and `code-def <function>` work fine. So on a Java / C++ / Swift project, `code-def` silently can't find a method even though it's fully indexed and `code-refs` finds it.

## Root cause

`content_chunks.symbol_type` is produced by `normalizeSymbolType()` in `src/core/chunkers/code.ts`, which canonicalizes only a subset of tree-sitter node types and lets the rest fall through:

```js
return type.replace(/_/g, ' ');
```

So node types land as space-normalized strings: `method_declaration` → `'method declaration'`, `method_definition` → `'method definition'`, `constructor_declaration` → `'constructor declaration'`, `field_definition` → `'field definition'`, `struct_specifier` → `'struct specifier'`, `protocol_declaration` → `'protocol declaration'`.

`code-def`'s `DEF_TYPES` filter in `src/commands/code-def.ts` only lists the canonical names, so `WHERE cc.symbol_type IN (...)` excludes every one of those. (The plain `'struct'` entry already in `DEF_TYPES` never matched anything either — C structs are stored as `'struct specifier'`.)

## Fix

Add the fallthrough definition forms to `DEF_TYPES`. Read-path only — no schema change, no reindex; it surfaces symbols already present in `content_chunks`.

## Verification

On a brain with an indexed Java codebase, `code-def <methodName>` went 0 → N, returning real `[java] path/File.java:line (method declaration)` definition sites. Class/function lookups unchanged. `bun test test/code-def-refs.test.ts test/code-edges.test.ts` → 18 pass / 0 fail; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Follow-up (not in this PR): qualified queries like `code-def Class.method` still miss because `symbol_name` stores the short name; matching the trailing dotted segment would close that.

author: brentru
body:
### Overview Users can change the polling interval of an I2C component. Some I2C components have extra settings which may influence sensor readings - gain, measurement time, resolution, read rate, etc. Currently, those settings align with the defaults from the example code (or the datasheet) and users are unable to set up these extra settings. This pull request, in conjunction with https://github.com/adafruit/Wippersnapper_Protobuf/pull/197 and https://github.com/adafruit/Wippersnapper_Components/pull/327, opens the door for users to configure these settings from Adafruit IO Web. ### How It Works #### Diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD Router("I2cController::Router()
Add arrives, buffered for decode") HandleAdd("Handle_Add()
forwards settings to driver") Configure("drvBase::configure(settings)
walks settings, matches key") Virtual("setTempOversampling()
virtual key → method hook") Override("BME680::setTempOversampling()
maps value, writes I2C register") Defaults("configureDefaults()") Router --> HandleAdd HandleAdd --> Configure Configure -->|settings present| Virtual Configure -->|no settings| Defaults Virtual --> Override classDef controller fill:#E6F1FB,stroke:#185FA5,color:#0C447C; classDef driver fill:#E1F5EE,stroke:#0F6E56,color:#085041; class Router,HandleAdd controller; class Configure,Virtual,Override,Defaults driver; ``` #### Explation On IO Web; * User selects BME680, "Advanced Settings", **Temperature Oversampling** and selects 1x. Clicks Create Component. * For BME680, the definition has a settings object: ``` "settings": { "temp_oversampling": { "displayName": "Temperature Oversampling", "default": 0, "options": ["None", "1x", "2x", "4x", "8x", "16x"] }, ... ``` * For sensors that support them, the `settings` are packed into the I2C `Add` message under `ws.config.Settings settings` where `settings` is a map of a string and the index (within `options`). On the Device; * For I2c components, the `Add` message arrives in the `I2cController`'s `Router()` function and is passed to decode in the model (we buffer this to avoid overwriting the stream) and `Handle_Add` is called. * Within `Handle_Add`, the array of settings is sent to the base driver (`drvBase`)'s `configure()` function. * `drvBase::configure` walks the `settings` by index (specified by the json's `options`) and performs a check for the key (specified by the keys within the json's `options`, in this case it is `temp_oversampling`) * drvBase contains `virtual` functions for each key mapping, `temp_oversampling` maps to `setTempOversampling` * The driver for the BME680 implements an `override` for setTempOversampling, which performs the driver-specific mapping and function call to configure the i2c device's registers. * If `settings` are not provided by IO, the `configureDefaults()` function will be called. * This **new function** in the drivers provides a separation between the transport/sensor initialization (`begin()` ) and configuration (`configureDefaults()`) and will likely needed to be implemented across all `drivers/`

author: fdcastel
body:
## ⚠️ Stacked on #161 — review that first

This PR is **stacked on top of #161** (the go-unifi SDK removal). Until #161
merges, this PR's diff includes #161's 14 commits as well as this PR's own 22.
Once #161 merges into `main`, those commits drop out of this diff
automatically and only the §8 work below remains.

- **Review #161 first** — the go-unifi removal is its own reviewable unit.
- **This PR's net-new content** is the 22 commits that add a third
  acceptance-test target (UniFi OS Server) plus an end-to-end reference
  network. Nothing here touches the migration.

## Summary

Implements §8 of the improvement plan: a third `TERRIFI_ACC_TARGET=uos`
acceptance target alongside the existing `docker` (default) and `hardware`
targets, plus an `examples/complete/` reference network and an end-to-end test
that applies it. The `docker` and `hardware` targets are untouched.

## What's here

**`testing/` scripts (L01–L03)** — drive a UniFi OS Server (Ubiquiti's
first-party Network packaging) as a test controller on a Linux host you
control:

- `install-uos-server.sh` — version-pinned (5.1.15), SHA256-verified installer.
- `bootstrap.sh` — first-run setup + integration API key; prints `UNIFI_*` on
  stdout. `ENABLE_FAKE_DEVICES=1` chains into simulation.
- `enable-simulation.sh` — flips `is_simulation=true`, adopts 1 UGW / 2 USW /
  3 UAP, waits for `state=1` + default-zone seeding.
- `reset-controller.sh` — wipes Network app state between runs.
- `verify-devices.sh` — CI-friendly device-count assertion.
- `README.md` + `CONTROLLER_FINDINGS.md` — usage, the firewall-zone hardware
  requirement, the github-runner finding, and the F-001..F-014 catalog.

**Test wiring (L02/L03)** — `TestMain` gains a `case "uos"`; `Taskfile` gains
`task test:acc:uos` and `task uos:bootstrap`. Existing `docker`/`hardware`
cases unchanged.

**`examples/complete/` (L06)** — the EXAMPLE_NETWORK reference expressed in
terrifi: `main.tf` (5 networks, 3 WLANs, 2 firewall groups, 3 DNS records, 1
client group, 3 reservations), `firewall-zbf.tf` (zones/policies/order behind
`enable_zone_firewall`, default off), `stubs.tf` (commented blocks for the
resources terrifi doesn't implement yet), `README.md`.

**End-to-end test (L07)** — `TestAccCompleteNetwork_basic` applies
`examples/complete/`, asserts an empty post-apply-refresh plan (idempotency),
destroys. Target-agnostic.

## Test plan / results

- **`TestAccCompleteNetwork_basic` — PASS on docker (4.9s):** 14 resources
  applied, idempotent replan, clean destroy.
- **UOS Server 5.1.15 (Network app 10.4.57), local LXC:** 92/92 of the
  hardware-gated + docker-runnable suites pass (WLAN 23, ClientGroup 7,
  ClientDevice 32, DNSRecord 11, FirewallGroup 13, Network 6). This is the
  evidence the `uos` target adds over `docker` — it exercises the real Network
  application.
- **firewall_zone / firewall_policy / firewall_policy_order** stay
  `requireHardware`-gated: the controller only seeds the default zones (incl.
  the `Hotspot` parent every user zone needs) once a real gateway is adopted,
  which neither docker nor UOS simulation does. Documented in
  `testing/README.md`.

## Decisions worth surfacing

- **No github-hosted UOS CI.** I built and ran a probe workflow 8× on
  `ubuntu-24.04` runners; the UOS installer resolves the invoking user from
  the runner's non-root `runner` account (audit loginuid / cwd owner —
  immutable under sudo, unaffected by `systemd-run --scope`) and points
  rootless podman at an unusable home. Five layered workarounds each cleared
  one subsystem and surfaced the next. Conclusion: the installer is built for
  a bare-root host; `uos` ships as a **local / self-hosted** target. The two
  viable CI paths (a self-hosted root runner like `ci-hil`, or a pre-baked UOS
  image) are documented in `testing/README.md`. The probe workflow was
  removed.
- **`examples/complete/` omits the `terraform{}`/`provider{}` blocks** because
  terraform-plugin-testing forbids provider declarations in a
  ConfigDirectory-applied config. The README shows the `versions.tf` to add
  for standalone/registry use.
- **The complete test passes on docker but times out on a busy UOS controller**
  under Terraform's 10-way parallel `networkconf` burst (that controller
  recomputes per-network with adopted devices). Bench-load, not a defect — every
  resource is independently green. Documented with the `-parallelism=2`
  workaround.

author: gorrdy
body:
## Summary

Two fixes for cross-device owner-lane rotation desync. Without these, two devices that rotate independently end up on different `contacts-N` / `cashu-N` lanes and silently diverge — visible as "delete token on mobile, desktop still shows it".

### `8505258` propagate full rotation snapshot across devices

`ownerMeta.value` used to be just `"<scope>-N"`. Adopting devices updated their local `*OwnerIndex` but never wrote a baseline / editCount / lastRotatedAtMs for the new index — those defaulted to 0. As soon as Evolu sync pulled the migrated rows into the new lane, `delta = currentRowCount - 0 = full migrated count` tripped the rotation threshold again, triggering a **second rotation on the adopter**, which the original device then adopted, and so on. Different devices ended up on different lanes.

Promote `ownerMeta.value` to a structured snapshot encoded as JSON:

```
{ index, baseline, cashuBaseline?, rotatedAtMs }
```

- `apps/web-app/src/app/lib/rotationSnapshot.ts` owns the encoder / decoder. Legacy `"<scope>-N"` values still parse (with null baseline) so old clients keep working.
- All three rotation paths (contacts+cashu, messages, transactions) now write the encoded snapshot. Contacts also carries `cashuBaseline` because cashu rides on the contacts index.
- The reconciler effect adopts atomically: index + baseline + editCount=0 + lastRotatedAtMs. Cooldown on the adopter starts at the rotator's `rotatedAtMs`, which blocks the cascade re-rotation window.

### `33f4bb1` heal orphan-lane data on owner rotation adoption

Adopting a higher owner index from another device used to leave rows the adopter held in its own (now-older) lane orphaned — the rotator only migrated rows it could see locally, so anything the adopter had pending in the old lane disappeared from the active UI.

Add three fire-and-forget heal callbacks that the reconciler triggers right after adopting a higher index per scope:

- **contacts + cashu** — derive both old and new owners from the seed, re-upsert every non-deleted row owned by the old contacts / cashu owner into the new lane.
- **messages + reactions** — copy nostrMessage + nostrReaction rows from the old messages owner to the new one.
- **transactions** — copy transaction rows from the old transactions owner to the new one.

Upserts are id-keyed, so Evolu's last-write-wins keeps the rotator's newer version of any row also touched by the migration.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run check-code` passes.
- [x] `rotationSnapshot.test.ts` (16 tests) passes.
- [ ] Two devices logged into the same SLIP-39 seed: change something on device A (delete a token), it reflects on device B within a few seconds.
- [ ] Manually rotate contacts owner on device A from `#evolu-data` — device B adopts the new index, heals any local data from its prior lane, no cascade re-rotation.

## Related

- Diagnosis from a real user: two devices had different `contactsOwnerIndex` / `cashuOwnerIndex` because `ownerMeta` never got a rotation snapshot written (legacy data, no rotation occurred post pointer-feature deploy). Manual rotation triggered the snapshot write and convergence happened via heal-on-adopt.
- Follow-up PR will add auto-write of a current snapshot at boot when one is missing — that completes the bootstrap path for pre-pointer users.

## Summary

Replaces hardcoded Rust toolchain version `1.89.0` across all CI/CD workflows with dynamic resolution from `toolchain.versions.yml`. This ensures a single source of truth for the Rust version and prevents version drift across workflows.

## Key Changes

- **Added dynamic version parsing step** to 6 workflows (api.yml, security.yml, api-smoke.yml):
  - New `Read Rust version` step that extracts the Rust version from `toolchain.versions.yml` using sed
  - Includes validation to fail fast if parsing fails

- **Updated all `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` steps** to use the dynamically resolved version:
  - Changed from hardcoded `toolchain: "1.89.0"` to `toolchain: ${{ steps.rust-version.outputs.rust_version }}`

- **Updated optimization status report** (`docs/reports/optimierungsstatus.json`):
  - Changed OPT-CI-002 status from `open` to `partial`
  - Updated evidence list to include `toolchain.versions.yml`
  - Updated next action and timestamp to reflect pending CI validation

## Implementation Details

The version extraction uses a sed expression that:
- Matches lines starting with optional whitespace followed by `rust:`
- Captures the version value (quoted or unquoted)
- Handles inline comments
- Validates that a version was successfully extracted before proceeding

This approach maintains `toolchain.versions.yml` as the canonical source for Rust version configuration across the entire CI/CD pipeline.

author: jeffreyyvdb
body:
## What & why

Audit finding (Medium): `RefreshStaleStatusesAsync` materialized **every** non-Pending, non-synthetic song *with its `ProviderAttempts`* and ran `ComputeSummaryStatus` — which JSON-deserializes each matched attempt — on all of them, **at every boot**, even when the enabled-provider set hadn't changed. For a large matched library that's a real memory + CPU spike on each restart.

## Change

Only songs **missing an attempt for at least one enabled provider** can compute to `Pending` (the sweep's entire purpose: a newly-enabled provider hasn't run yet). Every other `Pending` path in `ComputeSummaryStatus` is a transient rate-limit, which the retry sweep already handles. So the sweep now materializes just that subset via the existing `WhereMissingEnabledProvider` predicate instead of the whole non-Pending library.

In steady state (every song fully attempted) the query returns nothing and deserializes no provider JSON.

## Bonus correctness fix (audit Low finding)

`WhereMissingEnabledProvider` also excludes **manually-approved (locked)** songs. This fixes a latent bug: the old sweep had no lock filter, so it could flip a locked, fingerprint-only-matched song to `Pending` when a new provider was enabled — after which the orchestrator (which skips locked songs) would never process it, **stranding it in `Pending` forever**.

## Equivalence

The narrowed query is behavior-preserving for the sweep's purpose:
- "New provider added" cases (the reason the sweep exists) are all *missing-provider* cases → still selected.
- Fully-attempted songs can't flip (other than transient rate-limits, covered by the retry sweep) → safely excluded.

author: thefjk
body:
## Summary

The `/uberdev:goal` **orchestration layer** (`skills/goal-pipeline/SKILL.md` bash fences) had **zero runtime coverage** — CI only sourced `lib/goal-state.sh` and grepped the markdown (G6–G10/G17/G22/G33/G37 are all `assert_grep`). The entire loop (Phase-0 arg-parse + the bash≥4 resolver, the per-phase rehydration fences, the watch loop, the circuit-breaker firing sites, the merge barrier, Phase-3 convergence) shipped with no runtime test, so every wiring regression — including the sibling `/ubergoal`-audit defects — shipped green.

This PR **adds runtime coverage** by extracting the load-bearing bash fences from `SKILL.md` and **running them under the real shell** with `gh` / `claude` / `uberdev_dispatch_one` mocked. No production code is refactored.

## What changed

### New `tests/goal-pipeline-zsh.test.sh`
CI-launched under **zsh** (the SKILL.md fences' real Claude-Code Bash-tool runtime, where `BASH_VERSINFO` is unset); dual-launchable under bash too — the harness is launcher-agnostic and the extracted **fences always run under `zsh -f`**. A content-anchored `awk` extractor pulls each fence (robust to line drift, which matters for the mutation tests). Coverage:

- **P0 — Phase-0 bash≥4 resolver (#294):** under zsh a present bash≥4 resolves `UBERDEV_GOAL_BASH` and does **not** spuriously `exit 2`; with no bash≥4 reachable it **does** `exit 2` with the brew-install directive; arm-(a) is a clean no-op under bash≥4; the arg-parse fence parses issues+flags under the resolved bash (it relies on `$ARGUMENTS` word-splitting — which is exactly why the resolver publishes a bash≥4 interpreter).
- **P3 — Phase-3 terminal/convergence calc (#288):** does **not** converge while the rollover `queue` is non-empty (the #288 #1 queue-empty clause); **does** converge when queue empty + all PRs terminal; halts `queue_empty_not_converged` on a stuck PR.
- **W — one watch-loop iteration (step 2b):** the verdict-locator glob (`_uberdev_goal_glob_worktree`, #270/#290.2) finds a **worktree-mirror** verdict under zsh and transitions `pushed-reviewing → green` with **no `no matches found` fatal**.

### Replaced `goal.test.sh` G17 with a behavioural `--dry-run` run
The old G17 was a single-line negative grep (`dry_run=1.*uberdev_dispatch_one`) that **cannot** catch a real dispatch leak — the guard is an early `exit 0` hundreds of lines from any dispatch. The new G17 runs the real arg-parse + dry-run gate + `goal_dispatched`-emit fences with dispatch/audit mocked and asserts **exit 0 + zero dispatch calls + no `goal_dispatched` audit row**, plus a non-vacuous negative control (without `--dry-run` the emit IS reached). The G20 version-lock block is untouched.

### Wired into `.github/workflows/test.yml`
Wired exactly like the sibling `-zsh` fixtures: `zsh tests/goal-pipeline-zsh.test.sh` in the ubuntu `run:` block + an entry in the `ci-wiring windows-skip-list` marker block (it needs zsh, so the Windows job excludes it). `ci-wiring.test.sh` W1/W4 pass.

## Mutation verification (smoking-gun)
Each behavioural assertion was proven to catch its regression (revert fix → test RED → restore → GREEN):

| Mutation | Assertion that went RED |
|---|---|
| #294 resolver reverted to pre-fix `exit 2` dead-end | `P0a` |
| #288 `&& [ "${#queue[@]}" -eq 0 ]` clause removed | `P3a` (audit shows a false `goal_converged`) |
| #270/#290.2 `${~pat}` → bare `$pat` in glob_worktree | `W` (worktree-mirror verdict invisible → no green) |
| dry-run `exit 0` neutered | `G17.behavioral.no-audit` + `G17.behavioral.short-circuit` |

## Test results
- `bash tests/goal.test.sh` → **499 passed, 0 failed**
- `bash tests/ci-wiring.test.sh` → **5 passed, 0 failed**
- `zsh tests/goal-pipeline-zsh.test.sh` → **14 passed, 0 failed**

author: waleedkadous
body:
Closes #927.

## What

Reworks the dashboard's **Needs Attention** surface so PR-readiness keys on the **universal `pr` gate** instead of fragile builder-state derivations. Net **−45 LOC** (3 SPIR phases) — mostly deletion.

**Needs Attention = (A) ∪ (B):**
- **(A)** open PRs whose linked builder has a pending `pr` gate → **PR rows only** (never a builder standing in for a PR; a cache-missed/merged PR yields no row).
- **(B)** gate rows for genuine human gates: spec / plan / dev / **verify**-approval.
- plus the existing unaffiliated/human-PR (`REVIEW_REQUIRED`) fallback.

## How (by phase)

1. **server-derivation** (`packages/codev`, `packages/types`): `derivePrReady` reduced to the `requested_at`-aware `pr`-gate-pending check (drops the `bugfix && verified` fallback and the `pr_ready_for_human` field dependency — kills the #919 sticky-field hazard). `verify-approval → "verify review"` added to `GATE_LABELS`; `detectBlockedSince` unified on `Object.keys(GATE_LABELS)`.
2. **dashboard-surfacing** (`packages/dashboard`): deleted the builder-emit branch; `if (b.prReady) continue;` makes PR-ready builders surface only as PR rows; affiliated PRs use the gate timestamp (`createdAt` only for unaffiliated); `verify` styling (`gateKindClass` + `.attention-kind--verify`).
3. **remove-dead-projection** (`packages/codev`, `packages/types`): removed `recentlyMergedIssueIds` end-to-end. **Retained** `fetchRecentMergedPRs` (still feeds the recentlyClosed PR-link map).

## Shared-infra / VSCode blast radius (cc area/vscode — @Amr)

`pr` **stays** in the shared `GATE_LABELS`/`detectBlocked*` so VSCode (tree/toast/status-bar) is unchanged; the "no builder stand-in" rule is **dashboard-local**. New: `verify-approval` now surfaces as a blocked builder in VSCode via the gate-toast generic fallback (added a `builders.test.ts` regression-guard). **Open question for Amr**: is that the desired VSCode UX, or do you want a dedicated `GATE_ACTIONS` "Verify" action? (additive follow-up — not a blocker.)

## Verification

- porch `build` + `tests` green at every phase; dashboard `NeedsAttentionList` 13/13; VSCode `builders.test.ts` type-checks (Electron run = area CI).
- **Render-verified** the new `--verify` styling in headless chromium against the built CSS: `.attention-kind--verify` → `rgb(234,179,8)` (`--status-waiting`, == PR row), distinct from spec and from an unstyled control.
- 3-way CMAP per phase (Gemini/Codex/Claude); all REQUEST_CHANGES addressed.

## Relationships

- **#919**: this supersedes its Needs-Attention / `derivePrReady` parts — recommend descoping #919 to just the `verified → complete` rename.
- **#902 / #901**: `recentlyMergedIssueIds` retired.

See `codev/reviews/927-needs-attention-surface-prs-vi.md` for the full review, consultation history, and lessons.

author: cvolzer3
body:
## Problem

Coding agents that interact with PostHog currently must use MCP tools, which loads ~349 tool schemas into context upfront. This costs tokens and doesn't compose with shell pipelines.

Agents need a CLI that exposes the same operations as composable shell commands, discovered on demand via `--help` rather than loaded up front.

## Changes

Auto-generate a full CLI command surface (~349 operations) from the same OpenAPI → MCP pipeline that produces MCP tools. The CLI stays in lockstep with the MCP via a declarative manifest and conformance harness.

**How an agent uses it:**

```bash
# Discover categories
posthog-cli --help

# Discover verbs in a category
posthog-cli feature-flag --help

# Discover flags for a verb
posthog-cli feature-flag create --help

# Run the command
posthog-cli feature-flag create --key checkout-v2 --name "Checkout v2" --active true

# Preview without sending
posthog-cli feature-flag create --key checkout-v2 --dry-run

# Pipe to jq
posthog-cli feature-flag list | jq '.results[].key'
```

Each `--help` call costs a few hundred tokens of context vs ~100K+ for loading all MCP tool schemas.

**Architecture:**

- `services/mcp/scripts/generate-cli-manifest.ts` — emits `cli-manifest.json` from resolved YAML + OpenAPI inputs
- `cli/src/agent/` — Rust interpreter: manifest schema, request builder (17 transforms), dynamic clap command tree
- `services/mcp/scripts/generate-cli-conformance.ts` — drives real MCP handlers, produces request goldens
- CI gates: manifest regeneration in `ci-backend.yml`, conformance tests in `ci-cli.yml`
- `posthog-cli init --agent` — writes the steering block into `AGENTS.md` for agent discovery

## How did you test this code?

Agent-authored PR. Ran `cargo test` (all pass), verified `--help` output for multiple categories, tested live API calls against local dev. CI conformance harness asserts byte-identical requests between CLI and MCP handlers.

## 🤖 Agent context

Co-authored with Claude Code (Opus). Key decisions:
- **Fully declarative manifest** over per-tool Rust code — every MCP request-shaping transform is encoded as data, so adding a new API endpoint requires zero Rust changes
- **`get-all` → `list` verb normalization** — agents consistently try `list` first; aliasing avoids a wasted turn
- **Descriptions from OpenAPI** — tool and param descriptions flow from serializer `help_text` through the pipeline into `--help` output
- **`--agent` flag on `init`** — non-interactive mode so agents can set up steering without TTY prompts

author: jjstwerff
body:
## Summary

Phase 6.5 strict-CI (PR #2) surfaced ~13 warnings in \`arguments\` (12× \`v[i]\` may-be-null + 1× unused param + 2× field \"read but never defended\").  This sweep brings the package to **zero warnings** with **no \`.allow_warnings\` opt-out**.

## Changes

- **\`struct Args\`** — vector fields (\`options\`, \`results\`, \`positionals\`) marked \`not null\`.  Safe: \`create()\` initialises each to \`[]\`; writers only append/index-assign — neither path can produce null.  Silences the field-level \"is read N times and never defended\" warnings.

- **\`parse\` / \`has\` / \`get\`** — capture \`self.options\` + \`self.results\` into local vars (\`options = self.options;\` / \`results = self.results;\`) at the top of each function.  This enables skip-pattern 5 (\`if idx < len(vec) { vec[idx] }\`) which only matches when the vec is a bare local \`Var\`, not a struct-field deref.

- **\`parse\`** — every indexed write wrapped in \`if idx < len(results) { ... }\`.  Dead code in practice (indexes come from \`find_long_opt\` / \`find_short_opt\` which return -1 or a valid options-index, and options/results are kept in lockstep), but lets the parser see the bound proof.

- **\`parse\` mandatory check + \`has\`** — capture \`results[i]\` into a local then null-check (skip-pattern \"\`x = v[i]; if x != null { ... }\`\").

- **\`get\`** — return through \`if get_idx < len(results) { results[get_idx] } else { null }\`.  The else-branch \`null\` requires the parser fix from loft #231 (@P385) to type-check.

- **\`tests/01-arguments.loft\`** — \`fn on_verbose(val: …)\` → \`_val\` (unused param).

## Verification

Local build of loft carrying the @P385 + @P386 fixes from jjstwerff/loft#231:

\`\`\`
$ cd arguments && LOFT_DENY_WARNINGS=1 loft test
All argument tests passed
test result: ok. 11 passed; 1 file

$ cd arguments && LOFT_DENY_WARNINGS=1 loft --native test
All argument tests passed
test result: ok. 11 passed; 1 file
\`\`\`

## Dependencies

CI on this PR will be red until **both** of these land:

1. **jjstwerff/loft #231** — lands @P385 + @P386 in loft \`main\`.  The else-branch bare \`null\` (P385) and the text-nullable native return shape (P386) both need those fixes.
2. **loft-libs-core PR #2** (canonical library-ci.yml) — its \`cargo build --release --lib --bin loft\` infra fix unblocks the \`mmap_storage\` native-link error that was hiding all package failures.

Recommended merge order:

1. loft #231 → loft main
2. loft-libs-core PR #2 → loft-libs-core main
3. **This PR** → loft-libs-core main

After all three: \`arguments\` strict-CI is fully green; \`crypto\` already passes after #2; \`random\` needs PR #3 (or PR #1) for its separate bare-\`#native\` re-clean.

## Notes

- Tap/click was chosen over CSS-only hover so it works on mobile (coaches are often on phones) and matches the existing lightbox pattern used elsewhere in the portal. Happy to switch to a hover-only zoom if preferred.
- No data-model or schema changes — purely a presentational addition.
