## Summary

PR3 of the design-parity-recovery roadmap — restores CSS for the Overview tab card grid (per spec §4.3 — "the biggest user-visible delta of the roadmap"). 8 components ported to CSS modules; 5 vitest unit-test files migrated to `data-testid`; `.overview-card` + `.overview-card-hero` lifted to `tokens.css` per §3.1 lift-on-second-use rule (D22); first `pr-detail-overview.png` parity baseline captured.

After PR1 (foundation) and PR2 (PR Detail chrome), this is the third slice of nine in the roadmap.

## Scope shipped

**Module CSS ports (8 components):**
- `OverviewTab.module.css` — outer grid container (`screens.css:250-256`).
- `ReviewFilesCta.module.css` — `.overview-cta` parent + 2 production-only sub-rules per D18.
- `PrDescription.module.css` — `.overviewCardHeroNoAi` modifier (D14) + description body rules.
- `AiSummaryCard.module.css` — 4 active rules + 5 dormant handoff rules per D17 (explicit override of PR2 D9).
- `StatsTiles.module.css` — 4-tile grid with `flex-direction: column-reverse` (D7) so the large value sits visually above the label while DOM preserves `<dt>/<dd>` semantic order.
- `MarkAllReadButton.module.css` — `margin-left: auto` placement; visual treatment via `btn btn-ghost btn-sm` globals.
- `PrRootConversation.module.css` — vertical timeline rail via CSS-only `::before` (line, x=14, w=1) + `::after` (dot, x=11, w=7) pseudo-elements on `.prRootComment` per D13. 28px `padding-left` reserves the rail gutter.
- `PrRootReplyComposer.module.css` — outer container + `.composer-actions` only per D15. Inner composer classes deferred to PR4.

**Shared CSS lift (D22):**
- `frontend/src/styles/tokens.css` — appended `.overview-card` + `.overview-card-hero` as global rules. ≥2 PR3 consumers (PrDescription, AiSummaryCard, PrRootConversation) compose these literal class strings on their sections.

**Test-selector migration (D16):**
- 5 vitest files migrated from `querySelector('.x')` to `getByTestId(...)` / `queryAllByTestId(...)`.
- `PrDescription.test.tsx` uses module-imported `closest(`.${styles.prDescriptionTitle}`)` per the canonical hashed-class assertion pattern.
- Class-PRESENCE assertions on `overview-card` / `overview-card-hero` / `overview-card-hero-no-ai` — literal class strings stay on JSX as test seam + styling hook.

**Parity baseline:**
- `frontend/e2e/__screenshots__/win32/pr-detail-overview.png` captured (17.8 KB) in composer-CLOSED state per D21. Open-composer baseline becomes PR4's responsibility.

**Plan & deferrals:**
- Plan: `docs/plans/2026-05-30-design-parity-recovery-pr3-overview-tab.md` (14 tasks + D12-D23 deviations table).
- Deferrals sidecar: appended D12-D23 to `docs/specs/2026-05-29-design-parity-recovery-deferrals.md`.

## Plan deviations (D12-D23)

| # | Topic | Status |
|---|-------|--------|
| D12 | Production-vs-handoff naming divergence (4 components) | Applied — module CSS uses production names; ports handoff visual treatments |
| D13 | PrRootConversation timeline as CSS-only `::before` / `::after` | Applied |
| D14 | `overview-card-hero-no-ai` authored without exact handoff source | Applied — activates hero treatment on PrDescription only in AI-OFF path |
| D15 | PrRootReplyComposer scope limited to `.composer-actions` + outer | Partially applied — 6 inner composer classes deferred to PR4 |
| D16 | Test-selector migration via `data-testid` + literal-class retention | Applied |
| D17 | Dormant handoff AI-summary rules ported AS-IS | Applied — overrides PR2 D9 precedent with documented rationale |
| D18 | New production-only `overview-cta-*` sub-rules without handoff source | Applied |
| D19 | Handoff `.is-you` comment-bubble treatment not ported | Deferred to PR9 (requires logic change per §2.2) |
| D20 | Handoff `overview-card-head` top-of-card not reproduced | Deferred to PR9 (requires JSX restructure per §2.2) |
| D21 | PR3 parity baseline captures composer-CLOSED state only | Applied; open-composer baseline → PR4 |
| D22 | Lift `.overview-card` + `.overview-card-hero` to `tokens.css` upfront | Applied (originally a Task 13.3 review-time decision; promoted to Task 6.1) |
| D23 | Handoff `.ov-stat-sub` secondary-line slot not wired | Deferred to PR9 (requires prop + data plumbing) |

## ce-doc-review preflight passes

- `compound-engineering:ce-doc-review` on the freshly-written plan: 4 reviewers (coherence + feasibility + design-lens + scope-guardian); 16 unique findings synthesized. 2 Critical applied (D22 upfront lift, literal-class preservation for PrDescription tests). 1 Minor `8px → var(--s-2)` applied at preflight (commit `<post-push-sha>`). 3 substantive push-backs documented (PR2 D9 contradiction → D17 reconciliation; D14 modifier non-differentiation → conditional context clarified; AiSummaryCard cascade conflict → handoff-pr-ai-summary shape is the intended outcome).
- Preflight adversarial Sonnet sweep at PR open: 3 findings → 1 Minor applied; 2 Importants pushed back as false positives (cascade-winning module rule IS the handoff-`pr-ai-summary` shape per Task 7 design; AiComposerAssistant bare `ai-summary-chip` had no rule pre-PR3 either, so zero regression).

Per spec §4.1.4. Implementer captured `pr-detail-overview.png` after side-by-side review against the handoff prototype loaded locally. No unanticipated visual deltas surfaced. The visible deltas (content strings, font rendering) are within D12-D23 scope.

Per spec §4.4 — PR4 (Files tab CSS): largest component count (~13). The composer-primitive lift to `tokens.css` lands as part of PR4's slice, retroactively closing D15 / D21 visual gaps on Overview as well as the new Files-tab surfaces.

author: nwparker
body:
Fixes #2902.

## Summary
- Serializes remote workspace session patch writes per SSH target so overlapping local persistence events cannot both patch from the same cached base revision.
- Retries `stale-revision` once only when the relay reports a lower revision than the cached snapshot, which matches relay/profile reset behavior rather than a true newer remote workspace.
- Adds focused regression coverage for same-target write serialization and reset-relay stale revision recovery.

## Diagnosis
The status bar "Workspace conflict" maps to `RemoteWorkspaceSyncStatus.phase === 'conflict'`, which is produced when `remoteWorkspace:setForConnectedTargets` receives a `stale-revision` result from the remote relay. I did not reproduce the conflict on a clean first-create SSH flow, but I did reproduce the underlying stale-revision failure mode in a minimized handler test: two overlapping writes for the same SSH target could both read revision 7 and both patch with base revision 7. The first succeeds and advances the snapshot; the second can then become a self-originated stale write and leave the target in conflict, after which the renderer suppresses future uploads for that target.

There was a second compatible lifecycle path: after SSH target/relay reset, the main process can hold a cached snapshot revision ahead of the reset relay's blank workspace. Previously that lower returned revision was treated as a conflict; the fix retries once from the returned lower revision so a reset blank-slate target can accept the current local session without suppressing future uploads.

## SSH Evidence
- Built relay with `pnpm run build:relay`.
- Started throwaway Docker SSH host `orca-ssh-issue2902` from `node:24-bookworm`, user `coder`, port `127.0.0.1:22222`.
- Isolated Orca profile and CDP port for the before run: `ORCA_DEV_USER_DATA_PATH=/tmp/orca-dev-issue2902-ssh-workspace-conflict REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT=39417 pnpm dev`.
- Before fix, clean remote workspace creation did not naturally reproduce the conflict: sync status was `synced`, direction `push`, revision `1`.
- After fix, reset the remote/profile and ran with `ORCA_DEV_USER_DATA_PATH=/tmp/orca-dev-issue2902-ssh-workspace-conflict-fixed REMOTE_DEBUGGING_PORT=39418 pnpm dev`.
- After fix, created remote worktree `/home/coder/issue2902-fixed`; sync status was `synced`, direction `push`, revision `1`; remote snapshot active path was `/home/coder/issue2902-fixed`.
- Dirty delete path after fix: non-force delete returned `Worktree has uncommitted or untracked changes.` with `canForceDelete: true`; force delete returned `{ ok: true }`; store no longer contained the worktree; sync status advanced to revision `2` with an empty remote session.
- Remote verification after force delete: `test ! -e ~/issue2902-fixed` printed `fixed-folder-removed`; `git -C ~/issue2902-repo worktree list --porcelain` listed only the main worktree.

## Validation
- `pnpm exec vitest run --config config/vitest.config.ts src/main/ipc/remote-workspace.test.ts src/main/ipc/remote-workspace-patch-queue.test.ts`
- `pnpm run lint`
- `pnpm run typecheck`
- `pnpm run build:relay`
- `git diff --check`
- `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD`

Did not merge.

author: devsh25
body:
## Summary

Fixes the two issues reported on the exported PDF:

1. **It came out portrait, not landscape.**
2. **It was 12 pages of giant stacked cards, with cards sliced across page breaks (unreadable).**

### Root cause

Both symptoms had one cause. The previous version used `window.print()` + `@page { size: landscape }`. **Safari, Firefox, and macOS Preview ignore CSS print orientation** (only Chrome/Edge honor it), so the export rendered portrait. At portrait width (~680px printable) the dashboard fell below Tailwind's `lg` breakpoint and collapsed to its **mobile single-column layout** — hence 12 pages of full-width stacked cards, and the divided KPI band getting cut across the page boundary.

### Fix

Generate the PDF in-app with landscape as a **hard parameter** instead of relying on the browser's print engine:

- Rasterize `#dashboard-root` with **`html2canvas-pro`** (handles Tailwind v4's `oklch` colors, which classic `html2canvas` breaks on) at `scale: 2`, forcing a **1440px desktop viewport** so the dense multi-column layout renders rather than the mobile stack.
- Lay the capture into a **landscape A4 `jsPDF`**, paginating across pages, painting the dark background on every page.
- A `.pdf-capturing` class hides the interactive chrome (the button + filter bar) from the snapshot; the header banner and every card are included.
- The button shows a spinner / "Generating…" state while it works, and it's a true one-click download (no print dialog).

### Verification

Driven in **headless Chrome** end-to-end (click → download): the output PDF's `MediaBox` is **297×210mm (A4 landscape)** ✅, and a rendered page confirms the dark theme and colors capture correctly. (Local capture shows the data-error state only because this container can't reach HubSpot — on the deployed app with tokens, the cards render and paginate.)

- `npm run build` — compiles, TypeScript passes.

### Dependencies added

- `jspdf@^4.2.1`
- `html2canvas-pro@^2.0.4`

author: niovarchitect
body:
## Summary

Section 7 (Full Audit Viewer) Wave 1 opens the canonical audit read surface at `/api/v1/audit/*`. Self-scope only at sub-phase 1; org-admin + niov-admin scopes are intentional future-substrate per the section file's Next-Slices queue.

The existing `/platform/audit` + `/org/audit` + `/console/audit` routes remain LIVE — Wave 1 **ADDS** the unified per-caller surface those three admin routes don't cover: a caller's own audit chain, single-event drilldown with hash-chain refs, and HTTP-exposed hash-chain verification.

## What changed

**NEW [`apps/api/src/services/audit/audit-view.service.ts`](apps/api/src/services/audit/audit-view.service.ts):**

- `listAuditEventsForCaller(callerEntityId, filters)` — paginated `SafeAuditEventView` list scoped to `actor_entity_id == callerEntityId` AND optional `event_type` / `target_entity_id` / `target_capsule_id` / `outcome` / `start_time` / `end_time` filters. `ORDER BY timestamp DESC`. Pagination clamped to `[1, 100]` default 50.
- `getAuditEventForCaller(callerEntityId, auditId)` — single-event drilldown with `previous_event` + `next_event` chain references (audit_id + event_hash + timestamp only; both refs scoped to the caller's chain so they can never traverse another entity's chain). Enumeration-safe 404 `AUDIT_EVENT_NOT_FOUND` collapses cross-actor + unknown id.
- `verifyAuditChainForCaller(callerEntityId)` — exposes the LIVE `verifyAuditChain` primitive as HTTP. Returns `{ valid, total_events, broken_at }`.
- `validateListAuditEventsQuery` — validates `page` / `page_size` / `event_type` (against `AUDIT_EVENT_TYPE_VALUES` via `isKnownAuditEventType`) / `outcome` / target UUIDs / ISO-8601 timestamps.
- `SafeAuditEventView` projects the persisted columns; `details` projected raw because `writeAuditEvent`'s SAFE-allowlist already filtered it at write time (the read-tier projection is defense-in-depth per RULE 13).

**NEW [`apps/api/src/routes/audit.routes.ts`](apps/api/src/routes/audit.routes.ts):**

- `GET  /api/v1/audit/events` — bearer + `read`
- `GET  /api/v1/audit/events/:id` — bearer + `read`
- `GET  /api/v1/audit/verify-chain` — bearer + `read`

Wired into `server.ts` after `registerNotificationRoutes`; barrel re-exports from `index.ts`.

**Read-audit emission (RULE 4 + the CONSOLE_READ precedent):**

Every GET fires an `ADMIN_ACTION` audit row on the caller's chain with `details.action` set to one of `AUDIT_VIEW_LIST` / `AUDIT_VIEW_EVENT` / `AUDIT_VIEW_VERIFY_CHAIN`. **NO new audit literal landed** — reuses the canonical `ADMIN_ACTION` literal + `details.action` discriminator pattern (same as `console.routes.ts`'s `CONSOLE_READ`). Records only filter-key presence (not values).

**NEW [`tests/integration/audit-viewer.test.ts`](tests/integration/audit-viewer.test.ts) — 19 cases:**

- auth + envelopes (401 / 422 on bogus page, page_size over cap, unknown event_type, non-UUID target_entity_id, unknown outcome, malformed start_time).
- GET happy + SAFE: DESC sort + total + read-audit emission verification + per-row `actor_entity_id == caller` (self-scope proof at every row).
- `event_type` filter + pagination partitioning.
- RULE 0 isolation: cross-actor same-org excluded; cross-org excluded.
- Single-event drilldown: returns prev/next refs scoped to caller's chain + `previous_event.event_hash` matches the row's `previous_event_hash` (canonical hash-chain linkage proof).
- Single-event 400 `INVALID_AUDIT_ID` + 404 `AUDIT_EVENT_NOT_FOUND` enumeration-safe on cross-actor + unknown id.
- Single-event `AUDIT_VIEW_EVENT` audit-emission verification (carries the `audit_id` viewed).
- Verify-chain happy: `valid=true` + `total_events` for caller's healthy chain.
- Verify-chain `AUDIT_VIEW_VERIFY_CHAIN` audit-emission verification (carries `valid` + `total_events`).

## Local gates

- TypeScript baseline: **4 canonical residuals** (unchanged)
- Section 7 Wave 1 integration: **19 / 19** green
- audit unit regression: **23 / 23** green
- admin-routes + console-routes + audit-event-id-surfacing + notification-inbox + action-lifecycle regression: **89 / 89** green (5 files)
- no-leak guard: 2 / 2 green
- no-console anchor: 1 / 1 green

## RULE 13 substrate-honest disclosures

- **Self-scope only at sub-phase 1.** Adding org-admin / niov-admin scope is deferred to separate future waves. The existing `/org/audit` (org-admin) and `/platform/audit` + `/console/audit` (niov-admin) routes remain LIVE for those admin tiers — Wave 1 doesn't subtract anything; it adds the per-caller surface.
- **`details` projected raw** — relies on `writeAuditEvent`'s SAFE-allowlist at write time per the no-leak guard. Re-asserting that contract at read time is defense-in-depth per ADR-0002 + RULE 13.
- **Hash-chain refs scoped to caller's chain.** A caller cannot use `previous_event` / `next_event` to walk across another entity's chain (the query narrows by `actor_entity_id == callerEntityId`).
- **No new audit literal.** Reuses `ADMIN_ACTION` per the `CONSOLE_READ` precedent. Future per-Notification / per-AuditViewer literals remain RULE-20-gated forward-substrate.
- **Read-audit emission means every viewer GET creates an audit row.** Watching the watchers — operators auditing the audit chain are themselves auditable.

## What's NOT in this PR

- No schema changes.
- No new audit literals.
- No new RULE / ADR landings.
- No org-admin / niov-admin / regulator scope (intentional future-substrate; tracked in the section file's Next-Slices queue).
- No CSV / NDJSON export surface.
- No Control Tower UX (frontend).

## Test plan

- [ ] CI 4 / 4 green (Typecheck, Unit, Integration, Elixir)
- [ ] mergeStateStatus CLEAN

body:
Fixed the flaky test `test_number_discovery_start_and_stop` in `misc/discoverynode/src/tests/test_discovery.py`.

The previous assertion expected exactly five integer values and start/stop markers (`[None, '1', '2', '3', '4', '5', None]`). Because the test relies on `time.sleep(5)` to let background threads execute, slight differences in timing across machines could lead to a different number of events being processed. 

The new assertion logic extracts the generated events and ensures that:
1. The first event is `None` (start).
2. The last event is `None` (stop).
3. The items generated in between are exactly a sequence of strings from `"1"` to `str(len(addrs) - 2)`.

author: jjackson
body:
## What

The `nova_needs_auth_cache` FAIL branch in `bin/ace-doctor` called `mark_fail`, which is not a defined function (the helpers are `pass`/`warn`/`fail`/`info`). Every time that check fires it prints a spurious `bin/ace-doctor: line 1737: mark_fail: command not found` to stderr.

Surfaced today during a real `/ace:doctor` run that legitimately tripped the check.

## Why removing it is correct

The FAIL line is already emitted by the preceding `fail "nova_needs_auth_cache: ..."` call, and the end-of-run summary tallies failures with `grep -c '^FAIL ' "$DOCTOR_LOG"` over the tee'd output — not via any counter function. So `mark_fail` registered nothing; it was pure noise. The summary correctly counted the FAIL both before and after this change.

## Test

`bash -n bin/ace-doctor` passes; no `mark_fail` references remain.

author: sanrishi
body:
### 🛠️ Description of Changes
Hardened the `TaskRegistry` (`src/runtime/task_registry.py`) and API bootstrap sequence (`src/api/main.py`) against concurrency race conditions. Previously, `restart_honeypot_task()` and various registry methods accessed the internal `_tasks` dictionary without synchronization, creating potential data corruption and `RuntimeError` exceptions when tasks completed or registered concurrently.

**Key Improvements:**
- **Atomic Concurrency Control:** Introduced a `threading.RLock` to enforce thread-safety across all registry mutations and snapshot reads.
- **API Encapsulation:** Introduced a new public accessor `find_tasks_by_name()`. Refactored `restart_honeypot_task()` to use this accessor instead of direct indexing, effectively decoupling API-layer logic from internal registry implementation details.
- **Safe Shutdown & Cancellation:** Optimized `cancel_all_tasks()` to perform thread-safe snapshots, ensuring that shutdown sequences are atomic and immune to state drift.

### 🧪 How Has This Been Tested?
- [x] Verified that concurrent task registration and completion no longer trigger race conditions in the registry.
- [x] Confirmed that `restart_honeypot_task()` functions correctly via the new public accessor.

author: griptapeops[bot]
body:
## Problem

The `Version Publish` workflow failed when trying to create the release tag, with `'vmake[1]: Entering directory '...'.1.0' is not a valid tag name`. Root cause is broader than the tag: the version string was already corrupted in the committed library JSON.

## Root cause

The `version/*` Makefile recipes capture the output of a **recursive** `make version/get` call — both into a shell variable (`CURRENT=$(make version/get)` in the bump recipes) and into a git tag name (`git tag "v$(make version/get)"` in `version/publish`).

In CI, GNU make prints `make[1]: Entering directory '...'` / `Leaving directory '...'` to stdout for sub-make invocations. That noise got captured as part of the "version", so:

1. A **Version Bump (Minor)** run computed a garbage `library_version` and committed it to `main` (the corrupted value seen in the JSON).
2. The subsequent **Version Publish** run fed that garbage to `git tag`, producing the invalid tag name and the failure.

This doesn't reproduce in a plain local shell because make only auto-enables directory printing in recursive/CI contexts — which is why it slipped through.

## Fix

- Add `MAKEFLAGS += --no-print-directory` at the top of the `Makefile` so recursive `make version/get` calls don't emit directory lines into captured output.
- Repair the corrupted `metadata.library_version`, restoring it to `0.3.0` — the intended minor bump from the last good version `0.2.1`.

## Verification

- `make version/get` now returns `0.3.0` cleanly; simulated tag is `v0.3.0`.
- Simulated `version/minor` arithmetic correctly yields `0.4.0`.
- `make check` passes (format, lint, types, JSON).

After this merges, re-run **Version Publish** on `main`.

author: archlinux10-4
body:
## Problem (proven live in the SMART2 stress test)

A goal-only edit prompt produced two edits that QA scored **6/10, verdict `warning`**. The hard gate correctly **blocked** them (nothing below 8 ships) — but the fix loop **never fired**, and both edits were **silently dropped** instead of being sent back to the Surgeon for a fix. QA had caught a *real* bug (a signature change that breaks callers); the system threw the work away rather than repairing it.

### Root cause: gate vs. retry predicate drift
In `run_smart_pipeline_stream`, two places independently decided "is this shippable?":
- **Ship gate:** blocks if `verdict == "blocked" OR score < 8`.
- **Retry trigger (`_can_retry_qa`):** fired only if `verdict == "blocked" AND score <= 7 AND not _qa_feedback_for_retry` (i.e. one-shot).

A `warning` at score 6 satisfies the gate's block condition but **not** the retry condition — so it was blocked yet never retried. (The natural pipeline already does this correctly: it retries on `verdict == "blocked" OR score < gate`.)

## Fix
Introduce one module-level predicate, **`_qa_fails_ship_gate(qa, gate_min)`**, and route **both** the retry trigger **and** the ship gate (edit path + new-file path) through it. They can no longer drift. Behaviour now:
- Anything that would fail the gate is eligible for a **bounded** fix-retry (up to `_MAX_SURGEON_ATTEMPTS`), with QA feedback injected and **re-QA on the fix**.
- Removed the one-shot `not _qa_feedback_for_retry` lock — retries are bounded by the existing attempt budget.
- The gate remains the **backstop**: anything still below the bar after retries is blocked, never shipped.
- `None`/missing QA or score is treated as failing (**fail-closed**), matching `_gate_qa_fields`.

## Safety
- `run_natural_pipeline_stream` and `analyze_and_plan_stream` are **byte-identical** to PR #77 (asserted by tests).
- Gate decision is logically unchanged for normal cases (`not (blocked or score<8)` == old `verdict!=blocked and score>=8`).
- Diff is 4 small regions: 1 new helper + 3 call-sites.

## Tests — `test_pr78.py`, 22/22 (imports the real patched module)
- Shared-predicate truth table incl. boundary (score 8 ships, 7 fails).
- Fail-closed on `None`/missing/garbage QA and attr-form objects.
- **SMART2 regression:** old predicate did not retry (bug) / new predicate flags it for retry.
- Gate + retry + new-file paths all call the shared helper; old drifted predicates removed.
- Bounded-retry termination: never-improves → blocked after N; fix-to-9 → ships; clean → ships in 1.
- Natural pipeline byte-identical.

Next: capture a full **block→fix→ship** cycle live on prod to close the loop end-to-end.

body:
## 1. Summary

Resolves findings from a DevOps review of the Helm chart and the Prometheus observability surface, plus a frontend bug the review surfaced. Fixes two CRITICAL collector bugs that pinned dashboard metrics to zero, a Helm selector that mis-targeted the PostgreSQL pods, makes the ServiceAccount token mount configurable, and removes a dead `skipped` execution status that returned HTTP 400. 31 files across backend, frontend, Helm, and docs; all findings were independently verified before fixing.

## 2. Motivation

A review found the chart's PDB/NetworkPolicy/ServiceMonitor selectors also matched the database pods, the self-scraping collector filtered on `status` label values the producers never emit (so `K8sErrorRate` and the policy-execution breakdown were permanently zero), the SA token mount was hardcoded, and a phantom `skipped` execution status existed in the schema, API spec, and frontend filter despite never being writable — the frontend filter option actively errored.

## 3. Changes

**Bug Fixes**
- `helm/kube-phoenix/templates/_helpers.tpl` — added `serverSelectorLabels` (selector + `component: server`); adopted by `pdb.yaml`, `networkpolicy.yaml`, `servicemonitor.yaml` so they no longer match PostgreSQL pods. `deployment.yaml`/`service.yaml` refactored to the same helper (rendered output unchanged → no immutable-selector break).
- `backend/internal/observability/collector.go` — K8s error filter `status="failure"` → `"error"`; execution breakdown `skipped` → `interrupted`; removed the dead `annotate` verb term.
- `backend/internal/metrics/metrics.go` + `scheduler/policy_scheduler.go` — dropped the never-queried `status` label from the `execution_duration_seconds` histogram.
- `backend/internal/store/store.go`, `models.go` — removed phantom `skipped` from the execution-status CHECK constraint and model.
- `frontend/.../history/ExecutionTable.tsx`, `lib/types.ts`, `lib/statusColors.ts` — removed the `skipped` execution-status filter option (returned HTTP 400), type, and color entries.

**Features**
- `helm/kube-phoenix/values.yaml`, `values.schema.json`, `serviceaccount.yaml`, `deployment.yaml` — new `serviceAccount.automountServiceAccountToken` (default `true`, preserving current behavior).

**Refactoring**
- `backend/internal/store/observability.go` + frontend observability files + mock-api — `PolicySkippedCount`/`policySkippedCount` → `PolicyInterruptedCount`/`policyInterruptedCount`.

**Documentation**
- `docs/observability.md` — added a full Prometheus metric catalog; fixed two contradictory `cacheHitRate` descriptions.
- `docs/backend-dev-guide.md`, `deployment.md`, `feature-policy-based-scaling.md`, `frontend-dev-guide.md`, `api.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `openapi.yaml` (×2) — synced metric labels, the SA value, and the execution-status set.

## 4. Breaking Changes

1. Observability snapshot/history API response field `policySkippedCount` → `policyInterruptedCount`. The old field was always `0` (non-functional), so no real consumer behavior changes.
2. The execution-list `status` query filter no longer advertises `skipped` — the backend already rejected that value with HTTP 400, so no functional change.

## 5. Migration Notes

**No migration required.** The `metric_snapshots` table auto-migrates a new `policy_interrupted_count` column; the old `policy_skipped_count` column is left orphaned and ages out under the existing 3-day retention. The tightened CHECK constraint applies to fresh databases only (existing constraint is a harmless superset).

## 6. Dependency Changes

**No dependency changes.**

## 7. Files Changed

| Category | Files | Description |
|----------|-------|-------------|
| Bug fix | 11 | Helm selectors, collector metric filters, histogram label, phantom-skipped removal, frontend 400 fix |
| Feature | 4 | Configurable SA token automount |
| Docs | 9 | Metric catalog, label/value sync, SA value |

## 8. Related Issues

Not tied to a tracked issue.

- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] All existing tests pass (`go test ./...`)
- [ ] New tests added for changed logic
- [x] Documentation updated to reflect changes
- [x] No breaking changes to public APIs *(internal telemetry field only — see §4)*
- [x] No new dependencies added

author: divilella96
body:
💡 **What:** Introduced a `globalTesseractWorker` variable to cache the Tesseract.js worker instance globally in `mensagem.html`. Removed the `worker.terminate()` call at the end of the operation.

🎯 **Why:** Previously, the application created and terminated a new Tesseract Web Worker on every single image upload. This is an extremely expensive operation, as it requires re-downloading/loading the WebAssembly core, re-initializing the worker thread, and loading language data every time a new image was analyzed.

📊 **Impact:** Massive reduction in latency for subsequent OCR operations. The first image upload remains the same, but the second, third, etc. uploads will be processed significantly faster since the WebWorker is already fully initialized and waiting in memory.

🔬 **Measurement:** Upload an image with tracking numbers in `mensagem.html`. Time how long it takes to process. Then upload a second image. Notice that the second image processes almost instantly compared to the first, as the WebAssembly overhead has been completely eliminated.

body:
## Summary

Ships the public `/audit` page on linkedingrade.com. Users drop their LinkedIn "Save to PDF" export, see a preview grade above an email gate, and unlock the full report (12 section grades, top wins, three highest-leverage fixes) by submitting an email. The full report is also emailed via Resend and lives at a permanent `/audit/result/[auditId]` link.

User flow on `/audit`:

1. Drag-and-drop / file-picker PDF upload (5 MB cap, `.pdf` only).
2. `POST /api/audit` parses the PDF with `parseLinkedInPdf`, runs `runScoring` from the engine, persists the record, and returns a preview slice (Headline / About / Current Experience) plus the full report shape.
3. The full grade list is shown blurred behind an email gate. Submitting email → `POST /api/audit/email` attaches the email to the stored record, fires the Resend transactional email (fail-soft), and reveals the full report inline.
4. Below the report, the **Self-Assessed** block collects the 5 questions the PDF physically cannot answer (photo, banner, activity, recommendations, featured). Answers persist on the same record but **are never folded into the composite score** — the grade stays an objective read of what we can verify. The block is clearly labelled and visually separated.
5. `/audit/result/[auditId]` serves the same view as a permanent link (the URL the email points to).

## Architecture

- **`lib/storage/auditStore.ts`** — `AuditStore` interface with KV-backed (`@vercel/kv`) and in-memory implementations. Singleton accessor warns once if KV isn't provisioned. 90-day TTL. The in-memory map is parked on `globalThis` so it survives Next dev module re-evaluation between API-route bundles.
- **`lib/email/sendAuditEmail.ts`** — direct Resend REST call with an HTML + text body. Returns `false` (logged) when `RESEND_API_KEY` / `EMAIL_FROM` are absent — the audit pipeline must still succeed without email, per the spec.
- **`lib/audit/hashIp.ts`** — SHA-256 of `<pepper>:<ip>`. Refuses to hash when the pepper is missing (an un-peppered IPv4 hash is brute-forceable, so storing it would be functionally equivalent to storing the raw IP).
- **`lib/audit/buildPreview.ts`** — pulls Headline / About / Current Experience as the canonical preview slice.
- **AI-pending markers** — sections whose scoring depends on the AI judge (B3) surface their structural grade with a `*` marker plus the tooltip "Structural grade — qualitative review pending."
- **`next.config.ts`** adds `serverExternalPackages: ['pdf-parse', 'pdfjs-dist']`. Without this, webpack/turbopack bundling triggers `Object.defineProperty called on non-object` inside `pdfjs-dist`'s worker init when the route runs. Keeping it external matches the standalone smoke test.

## Privacy

`app/privacy/page.tsx` updated:

- Intro acknowledges the two surfaces (waitlist + `/audit`).
- New "The `/audit` page on this site" section enumerates what's stored (parsed profile, audit report, audit ID, email when submitted, user-agent, peppered SHA-256 of IP — never raw), the 90-day TTL, the Resend processor, and the deletion request path.
- The pre-existing "extension processed-in-memory" language is preserved untouched; legal-review markers stay in place.

A plain-language privacy note also appears above the upload UI on `/audit` and links to the privacy policy.

## Env vars the operator needs to set in Vercel

| Var | Required? | What |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `RESEND_API_KEY` | for email delivery | Resend API key |
| `EMAIL_FROM` | for email delivery | e.g. `LinkedInGrade <audit@linkedingrade.com>` (domain verified in Resend) |
| `KV_REST_API_URL` | for persistence | Auto-populated by Vercel KV integration |
| `KV_REST_API_TOKEN` | for persistence | Auto-populated by Vercel KV integration |
| `IP_HASH_PEPPER` | for IP hashing | Stable random hex string (`openssl rand -hex 32`) |

**Vercel KV must be provisioned in the Vercel dashboard** before production launch — without it the in-memory fallback discards audit records on every cold start.

If `RESEND_API_KEY` / `EMAIL_FROM` are unset the audit still completes: the record is persisted, the full report renders on-page, the page surfaces "Email delivery isn't configured on this environment yet — your report is still available at the link below," and a single warning is logged server-side.

## Tests

74 / 74 pass. New coverage:

- `lib/storage/__tests__/auditStore.test.ts` — in-memory CRUD + the invariant that `attachSelfReport` must not mutate `audit.composite`.
- `lib/audit/__tests__/buildPreview.test.ts` — preview slice always = `[headline, about, currentExperience]` in canonical order; gated count correct.
- `lib/audit/__tests__/hashIp.test.ts` — fails closed without a pepper; stable / distinct under expected conditions; `extractIp` prefers `x-forwarded-for`.
- `lib/email/__tests__/sendAuditEmail.test.ts` — fail-soft across four paths (missing key, missing from, non-2xx response, network throw); success path posts the expected Resend payload.

The previous parser tests (51) remain untouched.

## Verification

- ✅ `npm run typecheck` clean
- ✅ `npm run build` clean (routes registered: `/audit`, `/audit/result/[auditId]`, `/api/audit`, `/api/audit/email`, `/api/audit/self-report`)
- ✅ `npm test` — 74/74
- ✅ End-to-end exercised against a generated Profile.pdf via `scripts/make-test-profile-pdf.mjs`:
  ```
  GET  /audit                                                                   HTTP 200
  POST /api/audit                                                               HTTP 200  (auditId returned)
  POST /api/audit/email   { auditId, email }                                    HTTP 200  ({"success":true,"emailed":false,...})
  POST /api/audit/self-report { auditId, selfReport: {...} }                    HTTP 200
  GET  /audit/result/<auditId>                                                  HTTP 200
  ```
  Result page markers verified present: `Mir Quadri`, `Composite grade`, `Self-assessed · not verified`, `never folded into your composite`, `Highest-leverage fixes`, `Top wins`, `Save self-assessment`.
- ✅ Composite score on the result page === score returned by `/api/audit` === score the engine produces standalone (self-report does not modify it).
- ✅ With `RESEND_API_KEY` unset, `/api/audit/email` returns `{"success":true,"emailed":false}` and logs `[sendAuditEmail] missing RESEND_API_KEY — skipping email send for ...`. Full report renders on-page regardless.

**Screenshot:** the sandbox this PR was authored in doesn't have a browser available; please use the Vercel preview deployment (auto-built from this PR) to confirm the visual rendering against `./Profile.pdf` (or generate one via `node scripts/make-test-profile-pdf.mjs` after cloning).

## Scope

In scope (per task brief):
- `/audit` page + three API routes
- Resend integration with absent-key fail-soft
- Storage abstraction (KV + in-memory)
- Self-report checklist (recorded, never scored)
- AI-pending `*` markers (no AI calls — that ships in B3)
- Privacy page update
- Honest in-page copy

Out of scope (untouched):
- `lib/engine/*` — scoring rubric and weights
- `lib/pdf/*` — the parser (just merged)
- The Chrome extension repo

body:
### Motivation and Context

When GitHubCopilotAgent ran MCP HTTP tools, successful tool results were wrapped in opaque `AIContent` objects instead of semantic `FunctionResultContent`, causing LMs to interpret the result as missing and fabricate timeout errors (e.g. "MCP error -32001: Request timed out"). This affected all model families tested.

Fixes #5897

<!-- Thank you for your contribution to the Agent Framework repo!
Please help reviewers and future users, providing the following information:
  1. Why is this change required?
  2. What problem does it solve?
  3. What scenario does it contribute to?
  4. If it fixes an open issue, please link to the issue here.
-->

### Description

The root cause was that `RunCoreStreamingAsync`'s event-dispatch switch had no cases for `ToolExecutionStartEvent` or `ToolExecutionCompleteEvent`—they fell through to the `default:` branch producing opaque `AIContent { RawRepresentation }`. The fix adds explicit switch cases and converter methods that project `ToolExecutionStartEvent` into `FunctionCallContent` (with parsed arguments, tool call ID, and tool name) and `ToolExecutionCompleteEvent` into `FunctionResultContent` (with result content or error message). Additionally, transport headers (e.g. Authorization) are no longer leaked into the externally-surfaced tool approval request in `InvokeMcpToolExecutor`. Unit tests verify correct projection for success, error, null-argument, and complex-argument scenarios.

     These notes will help understanding how your code works. Thanks! -->

body:
## Resumen

Asistente conversacional con IA (Claude) para **Intergranel** que:

1. **Atiende clientes por WhatsApp** (Cloud API de Meta) — responde dudas sobre órdenes de compra, fechas de entrega, productos y montos, consultando el ERP mediante *tools*, y escala con un asesor humano cuando hace falta.
2. **Envía notificaciones proactivas** — cuando el ERP reporta un cambio de estado en una orden, el bot avisa al cliente por WhatsApp.

## Arquitectura

- **Backend:** Python + FastAPI
- **IA:** Claude API (`claude-opus-4-8` por defecto) con tool use y prompt caching
- **WhatsApp:** WhatsApp Cloud API de Meta (webhook de verificación + entrante)
- **Órdenes:** cliente de ERP/API externo con implementación HTTP real **y un mock en memoria** para desarrollar sin credenciales

```
Cliente WhatsApp ─▶ POST /webhooks/whatsapp ─▶ Claude (+ tools) ─▶ ERP ─▶ respuesta ─▶ WhatsApp
ERP (evento) ─▶ POST /webhooks/erp/order-update ─▶ plantilla/texto WhatsApp ─▶ Cliente
```

## Herramientas del asistente

- `consultar_orden` — estado y detalle de una orden por ID
- `listar_ordenes_cliente` — órdenes asociadas al número del cliente
- `escalar_a_humano` — deriva a un asesor ante reclamos o solicitudes fuera de alcance

## Probado (modo desarrollo, sin credenciales)

- ✅ `GET /` health, `GET /webhooks/whatsapp` verificación estilo Meta
- ✅ `POST /webhooks/erp/order-update` genera el mensaje correcto por estado
- ✅ Ejecución de las 3 herramientas contra el ERP simulado + recorte de historial
- ⏳ Llamada real a Claude no probada aquí (falta `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` en el entorno)

## Pendiente para producción

- Credenciales reales de Meta + plantilla aprobada para notificaciones fuera de la ventana de 24h
- `ERP_BASE_URL`/`ERP_API_KEY` apuntando al ERP real (ajustar rutas en `app/erp.py` si difiere el contrato)
- Mover el historial de conversación de memoria a Redis/DB
- Verificación de firma del webhook de WhatsApp (X-Hub-Signature-256)

author: ryderfreeman4logos
body:
## Summary

Fixes #246 — `mempal serve --mcp` advertised an invalid input schema for one tool, causing
Claude Code to reject the **entire** 30-tool list on connect (every mempal MCP tool became
unavailable after a reconnect).

Tool `mempal_phase3` exposed `inputSchema.properties.metadata` and `.report` as the bare
boolean schema `true` (schemars 1.x emits `true` for `serde_json::Value` fields). Claude
Code's MCP client validates each property as a schema **object** and rejects a bare boolean,
so it dropped all tools.

## What changed

- **`src/mcp/tools.rs`** — `Phase3Request.metadata` and `.report` (both
  `Option<serde_json::Value>`) now advertise a `{"type":"object"}` schema via a
  `#[schemars(schema_with = "json_object_schema")]` helper, instead of the bare boolean `true`.
  The Rust type is unchanged (`serde_json::Value`), so deserialization still accepts any JSON —
  only the advertised schema is now a valid object.
- **Regression guard** (`mcp::server::tests::test_no_boolean_property_schemas_in_tools_list`)
  — asserts **no** advertised MCP tool has a boolean property schema (every
  `inputSchema.properties.*` must be a JSON object), plus specifically that
  `mempal_phase3.metadata`/`.report` are objects. Runs in the default `cargo test` (pre-commit)
  tier. The test inspects `tool_router.list_all()`, which serves the exact same
  `Arc<JsonObject>` that the wire `tools/list` serializes (rmcp `schema_for_type` caches by
  `TypeId`), so it is a faithful proxy for what Claude Code sees.

## Verification

- Live `tools/list` wire dump (`MEMPAL_EMBED_BACKEND=stub mempal serve --mcp`) shows
  `mempal_phase3.metadata`/`.report` as `{"type":"object"}`, **30 tools**, and **zero**
  non-object property schemas across all tools (previously: both were `true`).
- Regression test fails on the pre-fix code (naming the exact offending properties) and passes
  after — confirmed by reverting the helper to emit boolean `true`.
- `just pre-commit` exits 0 (fmt + clippy `-D warnings` + test).

## Scope

Tightly scoped to the schema fix + guard. A pre-existing, never-compiled ~2720-line dead-code
block (`#[cfg(any())] mod tests_duplicate_conflict_artifact` in `server.rs`) was found nearby
and filed as #247 for a separate cleanup PR (kept out of here to preserve atomic commits).

Closes #246

author: pmi-topflo
body:
## Bug
Pushing an invoice to CINC failed:
> CINC createInvoice failed: Cannot resolve CINC StatusID for "PENDING APPROVAL".

## Root cause
`/management/associations/1/invoiceStatuses` actually returns:
```json
{ "InvoiceStatusId": -1, "InvoiceStatusDescription": "Pending Approval" }
```
Note the casing — **`InvoiceStatusId`** (not `Id`→`ID`) and **`InvoiceStatusDescription`**. But `getInvoiceStatusIdByName` read `StatusID` / `StatusDescription` / `Description` / `Name`, none of which exist in the response — so the name never matched and the id was never found, and `createInvoice` threw. (The endpoint, the management id `1`, and the name "Pending Approval" were all fine.)

## Fix
- Read the real fields: id via `InvoiceStatusId` (checking `typeof === 'number'` because CINC status ids are **negative**), name via `InvoiceStatusDescription`. Old field names kept as defensive fallbacks.
- Added a contains-both-ways name fallback so minor wording differences still resolve.

## Verification (live CINC)
`PENDING APPROVAL → -1`, `READY FOR PAYMENT → -2`, `PAID → -3`, `HOLD → -4`, `VOID → -5`. `tsc` 0 errors, build ✓.

Karen can now push invoices to CINC.

author: furuikeharuki
body:
## Summary

PR #289 で追加した詳細インタラクション計測 (`interaction_events`) は、これまで自前バックエンド (`/api/v1/interaction-events`) にしか積まれていなかった。本 PR では同じイベントを GA4 にも転送し、Realtime / DebugView / 標準レポートから可視化できるようにする。

- `lib/analytics/interactions_ga4.ts` を新設
  - 内部語彙を GA4 イベント名にマッピング (例: `impression` → `video_impression`, `play_progress` → `video_play_progress`, `pause` → `video_pause`)
  - 転送するイベントは `video_impression / video_play_progress / video_complete / video_dwell / video_skip / video_mute / video_unmute / video_replay / video_pause / video_resume` の 10 種
  - whitelist 方式でパラメータをサニタイズ (`slug` / `feed_session_id` / `feed_position` / `surface` / `rec_source` / `progress_milestone` / `progress_ratio` / `current_time_sec` / `duration_sec` / `elapsed_ms` / `direction`)。`metadata` の JSON ブロブは GA4 に流さない
  - `slug` を GA4 標準の `item_id` にも同送し、既存のアイテム軸ウィジェットでも拾えるようにする
  - 数値 (progress_ratio 等) は小数 4 桁、文字列は 100 文字で切る
- `trackInteraction` から `forwardInteractionToGa4` を呼び出し
  - バックエンド送信とは独立で、既存の dedupe / throttle がそのまま効く (= 余計なリスナを足していない)
  - SSR / `window.gtag` 未ロード時は no-op
  - `NEXT_PUBLIC_GA4_INTERACTION_EVENTS=0` で無効化可能 (デフォルト ON)
  - バックエンド未設定 (`API_BASE_URL` 空) 環境でも GA4 だけは飛ぶ
- 軽量スモークテスト (`apps/web/lib/analytics/__tests__/interactions_ga4.smoke.mjs`) を追加
  - web には正式な test runner が無いため Node 標準の `node --test` で実行
  - イベント名マッピング / metadata 除外 / null 値除外 / 100 文字打ち切り / 未マッピングイベントスキップを検証

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` (apps/web) パス
- [x] `npx next build` (apps/web) パス
- [x] `node --test apps/web/lib/analytics/__tests__/interactions_ga4.smoke.mjs` 全 5 件パス
- [ ] 本番 / プレビュー環境で動画を再生・スワイプして GA4 Realtime に `video_impression` / `video_play_progress` / `video_dwell` 等が表示されること
- [ ] GA4 DebugView でパラメータ (`slug` / `feed_session_id` / `surface` / `progress_milestone` 等) が想定通り入っていること

## Verification (GA4 側)
1. `gtag` が読まれている本番 / プレビュー環境で `/feed` を開く
2. GA4 管理画面 > 構成 > **DebugView** または **Realtime** > イベントタブ
3. 動画再生・スキップ・ミュート操作で各 `video_*` イベントが流れ込むことを確認

## Limitations / Follow-ups
- 既存 GA4 標準イベント `video_play` (= 内部 `play`) は別経路 (`trackEvent`) で送っているため、本 PR の対象外
- GA4 のイベントあたりパラメータ数上限 (25) を超えないよう、metadata は意図的に転送していない。デバッグ用に追加したくなった場合は whitelist を拡張すること
- GA4 側のカスタムディメンション登録 (`feed_session_id` / `surface` / `rec_source` 等を探索ディメンションとして使う) はダッシュボード側で別途設定が必要

author: theagenticguy
body:
## Summary

Two bugs in Python import handling left cross-module `CALLS`/`IMPORTS` edges unresolved, so a multi-file Python package read as disconnected islands in the graph. Both are part of the field-report's **Issue 1** (Bugs A + B) and are the foundation cross-module `context`/`impact` depend on.

### Bug A — multi-line parenthesized imports silently dropped
`extractPyImports` was line-based. A multi-line `from m import (\n a,\n b,\n)` matched the from-regex on the **first line only** with `rest = "("` → 0 names → the whole import discarded. black/ruff wrap every long import list this way, so most real modules lost their imports entirely.

**Fix:** `joinLogicalLines()` collapses physical lines into logical lines across an open paren (depth count) or a trailing backslash, before the per-line regex runs.

### Bug B — src-layout dotted absolute imports stub as `<external>`
`resolveImportTarget` only handled `./`, `../`, `/` specifiers. A dotted **absolute** import (`pkg.client` → `src/pkg/client.py`) never resolved, so it was emitted as a `CodeElement:<external>` stub instead of linking the real file.

**Fix:** `resolveDottedAbsoluteImport()` converts dots→slashes and probes the module at the repo root and under detected src-layout roots (`discoverSourceRoots`), gated to `namespace` import-semantics languages (Python). A dotted specifier that resolves to no in-repo file is still treated as third-party (external stub) — unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] **End-to-end on `ngs-research-agent`:** zero `<external>` stubs for `ngs_research_agent.client`; real file→file IMPORTS edges (`mcp_server.py → client.py`, `test_mcp_server.py → client.py`) now land.
- [x] **Bug A regression** (`python.test.ts`): multi-line parenthesized + backslash-continued + single-line-parens import extraction.
- [x] **Bug B regression** (`parse.test.ts`): a src-layout dotted import produces a file IMPORTS edge and **no** `<external>` stub.
- [x] `@opencodehub/ingestion` 604/604; `tsc` + `biome` clean.

## Relationship to PR #167
#167 fixed the `ingest-sarif` node-clobber that hid the host Function node. This PR fixes the *import resolution* so cross-module edges between real nodes actually bind. Together they restore trustworthy cross-module blast-radius for Python.

author: randax
body:
## Issue

Fixes part of #757 (recommended fix #1). Related: #750 (silent-drop symptom).

## Root cause

In the disco#info dispatch chain (`disco_info.rs`), `handle_muc_disco_info`
runs **first**, and unlike every sibling component handler (which guards with
`if req.target_to != Some(req.<x>_domain) { return None }`), the MUC handler
falls through to `get_room_actor(...).await` / `is_muc_room_jid(...).await` for
**any** target that is not the bare MUC service JID — including
`upload.`, `spaces.`, `push.`, `community.`, `extensions.`, `calls.`.

Consequences:
- A wedged `RoomRegistryActor` freezes disco#info for **every** component, not
  just MUC — matching the production HAR (7 silent component disco#info drops)
  and the per-connection frame-loop stall in #757.
- It is also a XEP-0030 routing violation: the MUC entity must not attempt to
  answer disco#info for JIDs it does not host.

## Fix

Short-circuit the MUC handler so it only consults the room registry for
targets actually on the MUC domain. Implemented as a pure, unit-tested
classifier:

```rust
enum MucDiscoTarget { Service, Room(BareJid), NotMuc }
fn classify_muc_disco_target(target_to: Option<&str>, muc_domain: &str) -> MucDiscoTarget
```

`handle_muc_disco_info` becomes a `match`:
- `Service`  → MUC service identity/features
- `Room(jid)`→ existing room-actor snapshot logic (unchanged)
- `NotMuc`   → `return None` (defer to the next handler; **no actor call**)

This isolates the `RoomRegistryActor.ask()` to genuine room JIDs and is correct
independently of whatever wedges the actor.

## Source-of-truth fix (from adversarial review)

Review surfaced a latent divergence the short-circuit would have turned into a
regression: `XmppServiceDomains` re-derived `muc`/`spaces` as
`format!("muc.{domain}")` / `format!("spaces.{domain}")`, ignoring the
`WADDLE_MUC_DOMAIN` / `WADDLE_SPACES_JID` overrides — while the MUC room
registry and spaces component are built from the override-aware `XmppConfig`.
Under an override, a room target on the configured MUC domain would classify
as `NotMuc` and silently defer. `XmppServiceDomains::new` now takes the
authoritative `xmpp_config.muc_domain` / `spaces_jid`; the disco router and the
registry compare against the same domain. Components with no override
(upload/extensions/push/community) are still derived from the base domain.

Non-blocking note (separate ticket-worthy): `RouterConfig`
(`waddle-xmpp/src/routing.rs`) still re-derives `muc.`/`spaces.` but is dead
code relative to the server; left out of scope.

## Tests (TDD)

Pure classifier unit tests in `muc.rs`:
1. `target == muc_domain` → `Service`
2. `room@muc_domain` → `Room`
3. `upload.<domain>` (other component domain) → `NotMuc`
4. `room@other.domain` (room JID off the MUC domain) → `NotMuc`
5. `None` target → `NotMuc`
6. `room@muc_domain/nick` (with resource) → `Room` (resource stripped)

Plus a dedicated XEP-0030 routing integration test asserting a disco#info to
`upload.<domain>` is answered by the upload handler (proving the MUC handler
defers rather than hangs).

## Follow-ups (filed separately from #757)

- #806 — promote PR #755's per-handler disco#info traces from `debug!` to `info!`.
- #807 — instrument `RoomRegistryActor` (mailbox depth, `.ask()` latency warnings,
  bounded mailbox / circuit breaker).
- #808 — design per-IQ `spawn` in the per-connection frame loop (stanza-ordering
  concerns need design).

## Verification

- `cargo test` (server) for the new classifier + routing tests
- `cargo clippy --workspace -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt`

author: jscatterplot
body:
## What & why

Adds a one-click **"This isn't right"** support report. When a depot user hits the button, the frontend captures the screen and POSTs it; the backend bundles the moment's context for engineering and renders the exact summary sentence:

> `User [ID] reported an error while viewing [Page]. System status at time of report: Tiger Cloud [Status], WebSocket [Status]. Last error log: [Error].`

The bundle is: the **screenshot**, the **last ~5 minutes of API logs**, and a live health snapshot of **Tiger Cloud (= TimescaleDB)** + the **WebSocket/OCPP server**. There was no support/feedback path before — and, critically, **no way to retrieve recent FastAPI logs in-process** (logs go to stdout only), so this adds a bounded in-memory log ring buffer.

This is a **backend-only** change. The frontend owns the button and the screen capture; the backend receives, assembles, stores, and delivers.

## How it works

- **`POST /support/summary`** (any authenticated tenant user) — JSON body `{page, user_note?, depot_id?, screenshot_base64?, screenshot_content_type?}`. Screenshot is base64 (or a `data:` URL), **not** multipart, so no new `python-multipart` dependency. Gathers logs + health, builds the summary, persists, audits, and schedules delivery post-commit.
- **`GET /support/summary/{id}`**, **`GET /support/summary/{id}/screenshot`**, **`DELETE /support/summary/{id}`** — `favonius_admin` only (triage + GDPR erasure).
- **Log ring buffer** (`src/observability/log_buffer.py`): bounded by count **and** age, thread-safe, installed on the root logger in the lifespan; never raises from `emit`. Known limitation: per-process, lost on restart, multi-worker only sees the serving worker's logs (durable `app_logs` table is the documented upgrade path).
- **Health** (`src/api/main.py`): `check_tiger_cloud_health` pings the **`ts`** pool (the existing `check_database_health` only covered Supabase/`static`); `check_websocket_health` uses the in-process `ocpp_server` when enabled, else an HTTP probe to the legacy handler's `:8081/health` (`WEBSOCKET_HEALTH_PROBE_URL`), else `"unknown"`.
- **Delivery** reuses the existing `report_email_client` / `EmailMessage` (Resend) — best-effort, off the request path.
- **Migration 047** `support_summaries` (TimescaleDB, BYTEA screenshot, `expires_at`).

## GDPR controls

- Lawful basis: legitimate interest (user-initiated diagnostics).
- Data-minimised to `user_id` (UUID, **never** email/IP); `user_note` / logs / error line are redacted (emails, bearer/JWT, secrets, long hex) before persistence.
- Retention-bounded (`SUPPORT_SUMMARY_RETENTION_DAYS`, default **90 days**) with an hourly hard-purge loop.
- Right-to-erasure: admin `DELETE` + `erase_support_summaries_for_user` (DSAR hook).
- Reads/erasure are admin-only; every create/read/delete writes an `audit_log` row.

## Reuse (DRY)

Auth (`ensure_tenant_mirrored`/`verify_depot_access`), `MaxBodySizeMiddleware` size cap, `write_admin_audit_row`, `ErrorCode`/`_build_error_response`, the `report_email_client` pipeline, and `_create_background_task` post-commit pattern.

## Tests

`tests/unit/observability/*` + `tests/unit/test_api_support_summary.py` — **67 passing** locally (ring-buffer count/age eviction + thread-safety + never-raise, redaction, summary builder incl. missing-error, screenshot decode/validate, health snapshot, and endpoint happy/sad/oversized/unauth/cross-tenant/503 + admin GET/DELETE + buffer integration). black/isort/ruff/mypy clean for the new code.

> Note: the container is Python 3.11 (the project targets ≥3.12), so deps were installed with `--ignore-requires-python`; a handful of **pre-existing** `verify_depot_access`/handoff tests fail on baseline too due to newer dep versions — unrelated to this change.

## Docs

`docs/API.md`, `.env.example` (new `SUPPORT_*` / `WEBSOCKET_HEALTH_PROBE_URL` knobs), and a CLAUDE.md architecture section.

> **Medium Risk**
> Stores screenshots and redacted logs (PII handling and cross-tenant log buffer exposure are mitigated but worth review); new authenticated write path and BYTEA persistence, with admin-only reads.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **context-aware support report** flow for the frontend "This isn't right" action: authenticated users `POST /support/summary` with page, optional note, depot, and base64 screenshot; the API assembles a redacted ~5‑minute log excerpt, Tiger Cloud + WebSocket health snapshot, and a fixed engineering summary sentence, persists to new `support_summaries` (migration 047), audits, and emails engineering post-commit via existing Resend plumbing.

Health helpers split **Timescale (`ts`)** from Supabase (`static`) and optionally HTTP-probe the separate OCPP handler when in-process OCPP is off. **Admin-only** `GET`/`DELETE` (and screenshot download) are `favonius_admin`; the create response omits `summary_text` and logs to avoid cross-tenant leakage from the process-wide buffer.

author: zachdunn
body:
## Summary

Pre-check before the Firecrawl go-live (#1248) found that `deriveMonitorSpec` builds a monitor-create body that is **malformed against the live Firecrawl v2 API**. A go-live `POST /v1/sources/:id/firecrawl/sync {enabled:true}` would have 400'd at `createMonitor` and created no monitor. The unit tests passed only because they asserted the same wrong shape against a mocked client.

Three defects, all in the **outbound** create spec:

| Field | Was | v2 API wants |
|---|---|---|
| `schedule` | `"every 6 hours"` (bare string) | `{ text \| cron, timezone }` object |
| `targets[]` | `{ type, url }` (singular) | `{ type, urls: [...] }` (array) |
| `proxy` | top-level | nested in the target's `scrapeOptions` |

Notes:
- The `events: ["monitor.page"]` value (the one assumption #1248 flagged as unverified) was **already correct** — verified against the live monitoring docs (the bare `"page"` is the crawl/batch webhook shorthand, not monitors).
- The **inbound webhook receiver** was already correct against the live payload (`metadata.sourceId` + `data[]` of `{ checkId, url, status, judgment }`); the ingest workflow re-scrapes independently and never consumes webhook-delivered content. No receiver change needed.

## Fix: adopt the official SDK's types (types-only)

Rather than re-hand-roll the shape, `FirecrawlMonitorSpec` is now an alias of `@mendable/firecrawl-js`'s `CreateMonitorRequest`:

- Added `@mendable/firecrawl-js` as a **devDependency** and imported the type with `import type`, which is **erased at build** — axios (the SDK's runtime transport) and the rest of the SDK **never enter the Worker bundle**.
- tsc now validates the request body against the real v2 API shape, so this drift can't recur silently on the next API change. (It already caught a latent `webhook` optional-access in a route test.)
- The tiny fetch-based client is unchanged — we borrow the SDK's types, not its axios runtime.

`deriveMonitorSpec` now emits:

```ts
{
  name: `releases:${source.id}`,
  schedule: { text: fc.schedule ?? "every 6 hours", timezone: "UTC" },
  targets: [{ type: "scrape", urls: [source.url],
              scrapeOptions: { formats: ["markdown"], proxy: fc.proxy ?? "auto" } }],
  goal, judgeEnabled,
  webhook: { url, headers: { "X-Firecrawl-Token": secret }, metadata: { sourceId }, events: ["monitor.page"] },
}
```

## Test plan

- `bun test` — all 39 Firecrawl tests pass across 8 files (the two `deriveMonitorSpec` tests were rewritten to the live shape first, watched fail, then fixed).
- `tsc --noEmit` — clean for `packages/adapters`, `workers/api`, and root.
- `bun run lint` (0 errors) and `prettier --check` (clean) on changed files.

Unblocks the go-live runbook in #1248.

author: potiuk
body:
## Summary

This PR adds an initial draft of a project-level security
threat-model document (`draft-THREAT-MODEL.md`) so that automated
security scanners running against this repository have a
maintainer-facing reference for which classes of findings are
in-scope vs. out-of-scope for the project.

The document follows the rubric format used by several other ASF
projects piloting improved security-model discoverability for
agentic scanners. Every claim carries a provenance tag:

- *(documented)* — paraphrased from public artefacts (this repo or
  the project website), cited inline.
- *(inferred)* — synthesised from code structure or domain
  knowledge; the PMC has not confirmed.
- *(maintainer)* — confirmed by an OpenDAL PMC member in response
  to this draft. (Zero in this initial draft.)

Draft stats:

- ~19 documented claims
- ~32 inferred claims (each maps to a §14 question)
- 25 open questions for maintainers in §14, grouped in 5 waves
  + 2 edge probes

§14 is the highest-leverage section: answering each question
either promotes one *(inferred)* tag to *(maintainer)* or corrects
the underlying claim.

## Why "draft-" prefix?

The file is named `draft-THREAT-MODEL.md` rather than
`SECURITY-THREAT-MODEL.md` because **this is a proposal for the
PMC to review — please correct, reject, or discuss as needed.**
Once the PMC ratifies (or substantially edits) the content, the
file can be renamed in a follow-up PR and a discoverability
scaffold (`AGENTS.md` → `SECURITY.md` → the model) added so
scanners can mechanically follow the chain.

## Scope

This PR targets `apache/opendal` only. The 3 satellite repos in
the PMC's scan scope (opendal-reqsign, opendal-fastrace-jaeger,
opendal-website) will receive their own draft-THREAT-MODEL.md PRs
in follow-up work; this PR is the main-repo pilot.

## What this is, and what it is not

This is **not** a security audit. It is a working triage document
— the reference a triager holds against an inbound report to
decide whether the report is about an OpenDAL vulnerability or
about caller misuse / a backend-side issue / an out-of-scope
concern.

The draft was generated by an automated agentic security scan
being piloted by the ASF Security team; the discoverability work
is independent of any specific scan run.

## How to review

1. §14 first. Each answer either confirms one *(inferred)* tag or
   replaces the inferred claim with the correct one.
2. After that, please skim §3 (out-of-scope) and §13 (triage
   dispositions) — those govern how a vulnerability report would
   be triaged. OpenDAL's "library-embedded-by-other-code" posture
   pushes a lot of finding categories to the caller; the draft's
   §3 / §9 / §10 are the sections that say so.

Reply edits / corrections inline on the PR, or to the original
`security@apache.org` thread, whichever fits the PMC's workflow.

## Summary
Implement internal System V function-call lowering in the x86 machine-code emitter. This now builds on the merged iced_x86 machine-code and ELF executable output already present in `staging`.

## Design Decisions
TAC `param` instructions are accumulated until `call`, then assigned to the System V integer argument registers in source order; TAC currently records params in reverse order, so emission reverses the pending list before register assignment. Function entries copy incoming integer argument registers into the existing stack-slot model, and stack-passed arguments remain diagnosed as unsupported for this MVP.

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
## What

`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/requirements.cljc` `token->evidence-slots` mapped `:trace → [:warnings]`, and the post-run fail-closed check (`evidence-slot-satisfied?` / `validate-evidence` / `validate-run-evidence`) treats an EMPTY required slot as "proof not delivered" → `:cannot-run`. But two trace-requiring assertions are HEALTHY precisely when `:warnings` is empty:

- `:rf.assert/no-warnings` (requires `#{:trace}`) PASSES on zero warnings.
- `:rf.assert/dispatched?` (requires `#{:app-db :trace}`) proves against trace DISPATCH rows, not warnings.

So once `validate-run-evidence` is wired into the runner (rf2-baah3), both would emit a FALSE `:cannot-run` for their normal passing case. `:warnings` is a FILTERED projection of the always-on trace stream, not a faithful presence slot for `:trace` — `project-evidence` exposes no general trace-events slot, so `:trace` has no faithful presence-of-evidence slot at all.

The same empty-is-healthy problem applies to `:hiccup-structure`/`:dom → [:renders]`: an assertion that legitimately asserts ABSENCE (`:rf.assert/dom-hidden`, a structural-a11y check finding no offending node) or runs against a tree that committed no render row has empty `:renders` while passing. The runner-selection PREFLIGHT already fail-closes these against a non-rendering runner; a post-run render-count gate only adds false refusals.

## Fix

Drop `:trace`, `:hiccup-structure`, and `:dom` from `token->evidence-slots`. The map now lists ONLY tokens whose slot is non-empty for EVERY healthy run requiring them — so an empty slot genuinely means "proof promised, not delivered": `:effects`, `:schema`, `:reactive-counts`, `:pixels`, `:a11y-engine`. The dropped tokens are always-on / empty-is-healthy; their proof is the assertion's own evaluation (the same posture `:app-db` already had). No behaviour change today — `validate-run-evidence` is not yet wired into the runner — but it is now correct before .31 wires it.

Docstrings on `token->evidence-slots` and `evidence-slot-satisfied?` updated; `tools/story/spec/017-Testing-Story.md` §Fail-closed evidence-slot validation token→slot block updated to match.

## Tests

New tests in `requirements_test.cljc` proving a `:no-warnings` / `:dispatched?` assertion on a clean (empty-`:warnings`) tape does NOT false-`:cannot-run`, a `:dom-hidden` absence assertion on an empty-`:renders` tape does NOT false-`:cannot-run`, the dropped tokens impose no slot, and run-level `validate-run-evidence` of `:no-warnings` + `:dispatched?` on a clean tape is `:ok`.

## Quality gates

- `cd tools/story && clojure -M:test` → 1241 tests, 3936 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
- `cd tools/story-mcp && clojure -M:test` → 172 tests, 861 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
- `cd tools/mcp-conformance && npm run test:story` → STORY-MCP MCP-CLIENT CONFORMANCE GREEN (exit 0)
- `npm --prefix implementation run test:cljs` → 4850 tests, 15890 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
- `bash scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` → PASS fast PR spine (markdown link/anchor gates ran + passed; mkdocs soft-skipped locally)

author: bjb2
body:
Closes #6.

## The bug

Reported by Axel on macOS. Starting the telegram bridge crashed with:

```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, posix_spawn '/Users/axelneff/.bun/bin/bun'
```

That path is `~/.bun/bin/bun` — the default install location for the official Bun installer. But the file isn't there. Most likely: Axel installed Bun via Homebrew (or asdf/mise/proto) after the deck started, and the original `~/.bun/bin/bun` was gone or moved. The deck server captured the old path at boot via `process.execPath` and kept using it for child spawns.

## Root cause

Two spots in the server spawn Bun child processes using `process.execPath` directly:

| File | Use |
|---|---|
| `apps/server/src/bridge-supervisor.ts:102` | Spawns the telegram bridge subprocess |
| `apps/server/src/index.ts:242` | `scheduleRestart` re-execs the deck server |

`process.execPath` is the path to the binary that started the current interpreter — captured AT PROCESS START, not "wherever bun lives now." `Bun.spawn` does NOT search PATH for `cmd[0]`; it goes straight to posix_spawn / CreateProcess and `ENOENT`s when the captured path is dead.

## Fix

New `apps/server/src/runtime-bun.ts` with `resolveBunExecutable()`:

1. Try `process.execPath` first — fast path, correct for normal users.
2. Fall back to `Bun.which("bun")` — searches PATH the way the user's shell would, finds wherever Bun lives now.
3. Throw a clear actionable error mentioning both attempts if neither resolves.

Memoized for the process lifetime (a working Bun binary doesn't move mid-process). Both spawn sites route through the resolver.

## Verification

- 4 new tests covering: existing-path returns, memoization, stale-execPath fallback to `Bun.which`, both-missing throws with clear error
- Full server suite still green: **177/177 pass** (was 173)
- Typecheck across all 4 packages: clean

## Files touched

```
apps/server/src/runtime-bun.ts          (new)
apps/server/src/runtime-bun.test.ts     (new)
apps/server/src/bridge-supervisor.ts    (use resolver)
apps/server/src/index.ts                (use resolver in scheduleRestart)
```

## Out of scope

- Periodically re-validating the cached path mid-process (a bun binary that moves DURING a deck run is too rare to engineer for — just restart the deck)
- Bridge UI polish to surface the resolution failure more clearly than the raw `posix_spawn` error (the new error message is already actionable; UI work is separate)

## Summary

### Cambios en \`/planes/:id/editar\`

**Mobile:** El select de Item estaba siendo aplastado porque Cantidad se llevaba ~40% del row con \`auto\`. Pasé el grid a columnas explícitas:

\`\`\`
grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_116px_40px] sm:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_132px_40px]
\`\`\`

El select agarra todos los píxeles sobrantes → en 430px de viewport ahora se ve \"Cofre Económico Pino\" completo en vez de \"Cofre Económi...\".

**Desktop:** El botón \"+ Agregar item\" flotaba arriba a la derecha del section header, casi tocando el divider y sin alinearse con nada de abajo. Ahora el section header se layoutea sobre el **mismo grid** que las filas, así el botón aparece exactamente en la posición de la columna Cantidad (132px de ancho), a la altura del subtítulo \"Item y cantidad incluida.\". El label se acorta a \"Agregar\" (sin \"item\") para entrar limpio en la columna más angosta.

**Mobile (continuación):** El botón se renderiza como una fila trailing DEBAJO de la última row, ocupando Cantidad + delete (\`col-end-[-1]\`) porque a 360px de viewport la columna Cantidad sola es muy angosta para \"+ Agregar\". \`hidden sm:inline-flex\` y \`sm:hidden\` togglean cuál de los dos botones está en el a11y tree por breakpoint → screen readers nunca anuncian dos controles \"Agregar\".

### Regla en CLAUDE.md

Agrego una nueva convención bajo **Style conventions** llamada **\"Dynamic-add form rows — select + one numeric input + delete\"**. Especifica:

| Slot | Mobile | Desktop |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Select | \`minmax(0, 1fr)\` | \`minmax(0, 1fr)\` |
| Numeric — quantity | **116 px** | **132 px** |
| Numeric — monetary | **132 px** | **160 px** |
| Per-row delete | 40 px | 40 px |

Plus las reglas de posicionamiento del botón **\"+ Agregar X\"**: top-right del section header en sm+ via mismo grid; trailing row spanning Cantidad+delete en mobile.

### Validación contra los otros forms del codebase

Tabla en CLAUDE.md que clarifica scope para futuros agentes:

| Form | Pattern | Aplica? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **plans/plan-form** (Items del plan) | select + Cantidad + delete | ✅ canonical example |
| **funerals/funeral-form** (Cantidades por item) | name/code + Cantidad (rows derivadas del plan; no add/delete) | Parcial — Cantidad ya usa \`!w-[110px]\`, no hay \"+ Agregar\" porque la lista la dicta el plan |
| **incomes/income-form** (Items comprados) | select + Cantidad + Precio compra + Precio venta + delete (stacked card) | ❌ pattern distinto (multi-numeric); top-right button OK ahí |
| **suppliers/supplier-form** (Teléfonos / Direcciones) | single text input + delete | ❌ no hay columna numérica para anclar |

## Pre-push gate

- \`npm run format\` → unchanged
- \`npm run format:check\` → ✓
- \`npm run lint\` → ✓
- \`ng build\` → ✓

body:
Qualcomm Inline Crypto Engine (ICE) platform driver now supports an optional OPP-table.

Add OPP-table for ICE UFS device nodes for LeMans platform

Testing:
* dtbs_check
* Validated on LeMans-evk platform


qcom-next PR: https://github.com/qualcomm-linux/kernel-topics/pull/1280
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260530-add-opp-table-for-lemans-ice-ufs-v2-1-2b46d3ac37d5@oss.qualcomm.com/
Signed-off-by: Abhinaba Rakshit [abhinaba.rakshit@oss.qualcomm.com](mailto:abhinaba.rakshit@oss.qualcomm.com)
CRs-Fixed: 4554448

## Phase C.2 — channel commits at the deferred leaves

Stacked on #14 (PR-C2a leaf outpoint resolver).  Three things in one PR
because they are tightly coupled and were validated together end-to-end:

### Library: the cryptographic primitives (C2b + C2c)

- `ctv_factory_build_channel_commit_tx` — 137-byte legacy serialization
  of a v2 channel commit: 1 input (the deferred leaf outpoint), 2
  outputs (to_user / to_lsp P2TR with the bare xonly keys), nLockTime
  pinned to 0, nSequence 0xFFFFFFFE.
- `ctv_factory_compute_channel_commit_sighash` — BIP-341 SIGHASH_DEFAULT
  digest computed from the commit TX bytes, the leaf SPK, and the leaf
  amount (the only inputs MuSig2 needs to sign).
- `ctv_factory_sign_channel_commit` — wraps `musig_sign_taproot` for the
  all-local 2-of-2 demo path (LSP holds both halves, demos and seeds
  the orchestrator until the real user is wired in).

### Library: the single-layer leaf outpoint resolver (C2d-library)

- `ctv_factory_compute_leaf_outpoint` — sibling of the hierarchical
  resolver from #14, for single-layer factories.  `leaf_txid = sha256d
  (legacy dist TX)`, `leaf_vout = user_index`.  Same one-call interface
  so the orchestrator does not care which factory shape it's in.

### Operator tool + orchestrator (C2d)

`ctv_factory_build` gets a `--channel-sign` mode that, given the funding
outpoint and a user index, emits a fully signed Phase C.2 channel
commit (the user's unilateral exit transaction):

```
ctv_factory_build --users 100 --slot-deposit 50000 \
  --funding-txid <T> --funding-vout 0 \
  --channel-sign --channel-user 3 \
  --to-user-sats 49250 --to-lsp-sats 500
```

`tools/ctv_factory_demo.py` gets `--with-channels M`: after the funding
TX confirms (step 4), the orchestrator signs M channel commits in a
loop and writes one JSON record per user under `channel_commits/`.  The
signing happens **before** the dist TX hits the chain — that is the
trustless guarantee.

### Tests

- 5 channel commit TX tests (layout, depends_on_leaf_outpoint,
  depends_on_amounts, depends_on_pubkeys, too_small_buffer)
- 3 channel commit signing tests (sighash_deterministic,
  sighash_depends_on_leaf_context, **sign_and_verify** — the headline
  round-trip: build → sighash → sign → verify against the keyagg)
- 3 leaf outpoint resolver tests (basic, depends_on_funding,
  rejects_out_of_range)

### What this PR does NOT do (intentional, next steps)

- Hierarchical channel-sign (needs both the hier-resolver hooked up in
  the tool and per-leaf tap-tree merkle root exposure for
  `activation-blocks > 0`).
- The dashboard-side reconciliation between signed commits and on-chain
  state.
- The headline 9001-user / 5-channel VPS run — comes after this merges.

author: bugsyhewitt
body:
## Summary

- Adds `--enumerate-runners` to `validate-token`, mapping the **pipeline-execution-host** blast-radius surface across all three SCMs — GitHub Actions org/repo self-hosted runners, GitLab group/project runners, and Bitbucket workspace/repo Pipelines runners. Distinct from the credential surface that `--enumerate-actions-secrets` maps: a self-hosted runner is the *host* those credentials execute on, so a compromised runner is a persistence and lateral-movement foothold; an org/group/workspace-scoped runner is broadest because every repo in the org can dispatch to it.
- Read-only and additive: v0.1 `scopes`/`user`/`admin` fields untouched; the `runners` array appears only when the flag is set. Normalized `{scope, owner, id, name, labels, self_hosted}` shape across all three SCMs. GitLab `is_shared=true` (platform-managed SaaS shared runners) maps to `self_hosted=false`; GitHub Actions and Bitbucket Pipelines list only self-hosted runners by design (`self_hosted=true`). **Decisive invariant: only runner identity and labels are surfaced — never a registration token, OAuth client secret, or any credential.**
- Reuses the shared paginator, scope guardrail, and rate-limit backoff; bounded by `--max-pages`; composes with every other `--enumerate-*`/`--audit-*` flag. Mock servers gain runner fixtures across all three SCMs.

## Why this over the planned options

The planned options were `--audit-dependabot-alerts` and `--audit-org-members`. A code/grep check confirmed both are already shipped (dependabot-alerts pre-30; `--enumerate-members` in Rotation 21). Self-hosted runners are the next high-value, three-SCM-parity audit surface in the same blast-radius axis — distinct from the `--enumerate-actions-secrets` credential surface because they are the *execution hosts*, not the secrets — with clean, documented, read-only endpoints on every SCM.

## Test plan

- [x] 13 new tests in `tests/test_enumerate_runners.py` cover normalized shape, the org-vs-repo `scope` split, `self_hosted` mapping across all three SCMs (incl. the GitLab `is_shared=true → self_hosted=false` rule), GitHub label reduction, the no-credential-leak invariant (no `token`/`registration_token`/`oauth_client`/`client_secret`/`value` keys ever present), e2e presence-only-when-requested, composition with the full `--enumerate-*`/`--audit-*` family, the scope-guardrail gate (exit 2), and `--help` documentation.
- [x] Full suite: **416 passing (403 baseline + 13 new), zero regressions**.
- [x] README updated with a "Self-hosted runner enumeration" subsection.
- [x] POST_V01.md updated with the shipped-status entry for Rotation 30.

author: mike-thompson-day8
body:
@
## What

`record-result-map` (`tools/story/src/re_frame/story/runtime.cljc`) assembled the unified run-result WITHOUT passing the `:unmet` slot that `result/run-result` accepts, so the run-state's `:cannot-run` refusals never reached the unified verdict. A DOM-skip-only variant on the headless JVM therefore aggregated to `:pass` (vacuous green) via `story/is` + Test mode — while `runner/finish`'s run-state correctly reported `:cannot-run` by inspecting the same per-step `:skipped?` / `:cannot-run?` results. Consumers disagreed → a resurfaced false-GREEN for DOM assertions under the default headless runner, the exact class rf2-5x1wt.19 set out to kill (spec/017 §Unified run result: "a run whose only unmet expectations are `:cannot-run` is itself `:cannot-run`").

## Fix

- `runner.cljc` — new pure helper `run-state-refusals`: projects a settled run-state's `:cannot-run` step-results (the SAME `cannot-run-step?` step-results `finish` reads) into the `{:status :cannot-run :unit :reason :message}` refusal shape the unified `:unmet` slot folds. One bridge from run-state truth to the unified result, so the two cannot disagree.
- `runtime.cljc` — `record-result-map` reads `runner-events/current-state` for the variant and threads `run-state-refusals` into `result/run-result`'s existing `:unmet` parameter. `aggregate-status` already folds a non-empty `:unmet` into `:cannot-run`, and `result/run-result` already surfaces it on `:cannot-run`. Degrades to an empty `:unmet` when there is no run-state (e.g. the error / loader-incomplete paths).

No change to `evidence.cljc` / `requirements.cljc` (sibling workers' lanes) or `ui/**`. No new test-only require into a production ns. The refusal predicate reuses the existing `runner/cannot-run-step?` semantics — no new (over-broad) predicate.

## Regression

`assert-dom-skipped-unified-result-is-cannot-run` exercises the UNIFIED-result PATH: `(:status @(story/run-variant <dom-skip-variant>))` is `:cannot-run` (not `:pass`), `:cannot-run` slot is populated, and `story/result-passed?` is false. The existing `assert-dom-skipped-on-jvm-is-cannot-run` discarded the result map and checked only `run-blocking`'s run-state, which is why this slipped through. Confirmed: the new test FAILS pre-fix (3 assertions: `:status` reads `:pass`, `:cannot-run` is nil, `result-passed?` is true) and PASSES post-fix.

## Quality gates

- `tools/story` `clojure -M:test` — 1237 tests, 3925 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
- `tools/story-mcp` `clojure -M:test` — 172 tests, 861 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
- `tools/mcp-conformance` `npm run test:story` — STORY-MCP CONFORMANCE GREEN (exit 0, 13 checks)
- `implementation` `npm run test:cljs` — 4865 tests, 15925 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors
- `scripts/test-fast-pr.sh` — PASS fast PR spine
